entries.text:
## The rules (these always apply)

The reason behind every rule is in `site/src/data/decisions.ts` (the site’s Rules & decisions page).
When a design and the system disagree, check it first; when a rule changes, update it there too.

**Type and colour**
- **Typography:** DM Sans only, through the 12 type tokens (`<Text variant>` / `EqualTheme.type`).
  Nothing is set in Lora, Roboto, the system font or any other font, not even in system mocks (status
  bar clock, dialer). Weights: 400, 500, 600 (SemiBold) and 700.
- **Colour:** only tokens. Never put a hex value in a component. Colours follow the Figma library’s
  “Colours” set: text black 80 / 60 / 40 / 20 % (primary, secondary, placeholder, disabled), strokes
  black 5 / 8 / 32 %, page `#FAFAFA`. A colour at x % is written as the colour-guide colour plus
  opacity: `"{brand.green} @ 36%"`. One-off greys snap to the text colours; readable text stays ≥ 4.5:1
  (40 % is for placeholders only). Every token needs a `why` that states its purpose.
  - **New colour:** add it to `tokens/tokens.json` with `"derived": true` and a `"why"`, give it light
    and dark values, and check text pairs for AA (4.5:1). Decide colours yourself; don't ask for
    sign-off.
- **Dark mode:** every component and screen works in light and dark. In dark, every green is lime
  (#BAFF29): accents use lime itself, green-tinted surfaces are re-hued to lime, and anything on lime
  is `text/on-action` (black), never white.

**Structure**
- **Atoms first:** every visible leaf is an atom (`Text`, `Icon`, `Emoji`, `Asset`, `Button`…), never
  raw markup with a typography class. Molecules combine atoms; organisms combine molecules. Set a new
  component's level in `site/src/registry/levels.ts` so Trace can show it.
- **Radii:** whole numbers only (2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 18, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 50, 54, 80, 100, full). The Experiments page is not a source for anything.

**Icons and images**
- **Action cards:** the grey body sits on a white card (never a green card), and every CTA row is
  emoji + label (📤 Send, ✏️ Edit, 👍 Confirm, 🗑️ Delete).
- **Icons:** flat icons are Material Symbols (`scripts/build-icons.mjs`, then `npm run icons`). Action
  chips use emoji, sized to the label font size.
- **Images:** the only images are supplied assets in `assets/`. Everything else is code: logos, seals,
  patterns, rings, progress bars, badges. Never crop an image; trimming transparent margins is fine.
- **Premium (monetization) surfaces:** perk icons are *filled* Material Symbols at 16 dp, painted
  with the gold radial gradient `premium-icon/start` → `premium-icon/end` (`<PremiumIcon>` /
  `PremiumIcon`). Light premium cards sit on the `premium-glow` art; dark ones use the coded
  black-gold gradient. Gold CTAs use `gradient/cta-gold`. Gold (buttons, text, badges) is only for subscription surfaces:
  paywall, plan, renewal, payment. Most monetization values (price, coupon, copy, entry point) are experiments: keep them as props.
- **Mascots:** the green mascot illustrations are generated to order. When a screen needs a new one,
  ask for it and show a placeholder.

**Android frame and chrome**
- **Frame:** 390 × 800 dp. Extend only vertically (`StagePhone.height` / `ANDROID_FRAME` on web,
  `EqualFrameWidthDp` / `EqualFrameHeightDp` in Compose).
- **Status bar:** Material 3, 52 dp. Text fields have 12 dp corners.
- **Avatars:** free users get the plain bust; paid users (Unlimited) get the gold background and ring
  (`tier: 'free' | 'paid'`). Saved contacts show their initials on the light-blue disc with the person
  badge at the bottom-right (the signifier for a known contact); unknown and business callers use
  category art.
- **The green orb** (nav FAB) opens the assistant sheet (Global MYA, `AssistantSheet`) on any screen.
  Requests become a short task conversation that ends in a result to confirm. Don't draw the system
  keyboard; just lift the input above it.
- **Call Handling** lives under You → Your assistant. Ask for a permission only at the step that
  needs it. Android draws notifications: `CallNotification` only fills the shell (who, what they want,
  Takeover first), and the wallpaper behind it in docs is coded.
- **Dark-mode You tab:** the cream-gold profile header stays light (its content renders with light
  tokens) as a panel with rounded bottom corners; the status bar sits on the gold.

- **Text inputs that can send:** show the mic while empty and the send arrow as soon as there is text.

**Engineering**
- **Stack:** business logic is Kotlin, UI is Compose, and animations are Lottie JSON (`assets/lottie/`,
  `<Lottie>` / `EqualLottie`). Respect reduced motion everywhere.
- **Experiments are props, not forks.** The Android team A/B tests monetization, so price, copy,
  coupon, entry touchpoint and similar knobs are props on the same screen.
- **Paywall experiments** (`MonetizationExperiments.tsx`): touchpoints and payment states are props on
  Home / Chat / Paywall (`planExpired`, `homeNotice`, `official`, `lockedActions`, `paywallSheet`,
  `paymentProcessing`, `PaymentResultScreen`). While a payment is processing, every surface says so
  and the paywall CTA is disabled.

entries.text:
## Where things live

| What | Web | Android |
|---|---|---|
| Tokens (generated) | `web/src/tokens/` | `compose/.../tokens/EqualTokens.kt` |
| Components | `web/src/components/<Name>.tsx` + `.css`, exported from `web/src/index.ts` | `compose/equal-ds/src/main/java/ai/equal/ds/components/` |
| Screens | `web/src/screens/*.tsx` | `compose/.../catalog/*.kt` |
| Assets | `assets/<name>.webp\|svg` + `web/src/foundations/Asset.tsx` | `res/drawable-xxxhdpi/ds_asset_*.webp`, `EqualAssets` |
| Docs page per component | `site/src/registry/components.tsx` | snippets in `compose/equal-ds/src/debug/java/ai/equal/ds/snippets/` |
| Flow pages | `site/src/pages/Flow.tsx` + `site/src/app/nav.ts` + `site/src/pages/Screens.tsx` | snippet group `flow-<id>` |

entries.text:
## Recipe: a new flow from a design (PDF, Figma frames or screenshots)

1. **Read the design fully.** Render PDFs at high resolution (`pdftoppm -r 100`) and crop each region.
   List every screen state, every component and every image.
2. **Map it to the system.** For each element, find the existing component in `llms-full.txt`. Only
   build a new component when nothing fits, or extend one with a prop.
3. **List the assets.** Split them into images to supply (3D art, illustrations, mascots) and things to
   code. Ask the designer for any images that are missing. Until they arrive, `<Asset>` shows a
   checkerboard placeholder.
4. **Add assets.**
   - PNG/WebP: a transparent file at least 2000 px into `assets/source/<name>.png`; add its display size
     to `SIZES` in `scripts/build-assets.py`; run `npm run assets`.
   - Register it in `Asset.tsx` (`assetNames` + `assetUsage`) and in `EqualAssets`.
   - SVG: `assets/<name>.svg` for web, and a VectorDrawable at `res/drawable/ds_asset_<name>.xml` for Android.
5. **Tokens:** add any new colours or gradients to `tokens/tokens.json`, then run `npm run tokens`.
6. **Web components:** add a `.tsx` + `.css` pair using only tokens, export it, and give it a docs entry in
   `site/src/registry/components.tsx`: examples with `code`, props, tokens, and do / don't. Add its
   anatomy (parts in reading order) and accessibility (Role, Name, Keyboard, Touch target, Contrast,
   State, Motion, for web and Android, plus known gaps) to `site/src/registry/a11y.json`.
7. **Screens:** add props to the revamped screens, or a new screen in `web/src/screens/`.
8. **Flow page:** add the flow to `Flow.tsx`, with states (`key`, `label`, `render`, `code`, and
   `height` when the screen is taller than 800), plus steps and the source. Add it to `nav.ts` and the
   Screens overview cards.
9. **Android:** mirror every component and screen in Compose. Add a snippet for every docs example and
   flow state: `// snippet: <doc id> / <example title>` or `// snippet: flow-<id> / <state key>`.
10. **Verify** with the commands below, and look at every state in light and dark on the site.

entries.name: rules/commands
entries.title: Commands
entries.summary: ```bash npm run site # docs site at http://localhost:5190 (tokens + snippets + llms first) npm run tokens # tokens.json → web + Compose npm run icons # icon manifest → web + Compose npm run assets # assets/source → web webp + Compose drawable-xxxhdpi npm run llms # regenerate sit
entries.text:
## Commands

```bash
npm run site          # docs site at http://localhost:5190 (tokens + snippets + llms first)
npm run tokens        # tokens.json → web + Compose
npm run icons         # icon manifest → web + Compose
npm run assets        # assets/source → web webp + Compose drawable-xxxhdpi
npm run llms          # regenerate site/public/llms*.txt and the Claude skill zip
npx tsc --noEmit      # web typecheck
node scripts/build-snippets.mjs --check   # every docs example has Compose code
cd compose && JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@17 ANDROID_HOME=/opt/homebrew/share/android-commandlinetools ./gradlew :equal-ds:compileDebugKotlin :equal-ds:assembleRelease :equal-ds:lintDebug
```

Done means: typecheck clean, `--check` passes, Gradle BUILD SUCCESSFUL, and lint reports
"0 errors, 0 warnings" in `compose/equal-ds/build/reports/lint-results-debug.txt`.

entries.name: decisions/principles
entries.title: Principles
entries.summary: - **One token file feeds web and Android.** Why: If a value lives in two places it drifts. tokens.json generates the CSS, the TS and the Kotlin, so a change lands on both platforms at once and nobody hand-copies hex values. (Source: Engineering) - **Experiments are props on one s
entries.text:
## Principles

- **One token file feeds web and Android.** Why: If a value lives in two places it drifts. tokens.json generates the CSS, the TS and the Kotlin, so a change lands on both platforms at once and nobody hand-copies hex values. (Source: Engineering)
- **Experiments are props on one screen, never forks.** Why: The Android team A/B tests monetization constantly (price, copy, entry point, layout). A forked screen per variant would multiply bugs and fall out of sync; a prop keeps every variant on the same, tested code. (Source: Product: Android runs monetization experiments)
- **Only supplied art is an image; everything else is code.** Why: Coded logos, seals, rings, badges and progress bars stay sharp at any size, follow light and dark automatically and weigh nothing. Images are reserved for 3D art and illustrations nobody can draw in code. (Source: Design direction)
- **Never crop supplied art.** Why: Designers compose the transparent padding on purpose (glow, shadow, breathing room). Cropping changes the art; only fully transparent margins are trimmed when an asset is built. (Source: Design direction)
- **Colours that aren’t in the colour guide are marked “derived”.** Why: The colour guide doesn’t cover every surface the screens use. Marking derived tokens keeps it clear which values came from the guide and which were measured from screens, so design can review them in one place. (Source: Design: colour guide gaps)

entries.title: Colour & type

entries.text:
## Colour & type

- **Nothing comes from the Figma “Experiments” page.** Why: It holds explorations that are not decided. Colours, radii, type and components are taken only from the other pages (Updated UI, Monetization, Global MYA, Preset Instruction…). (Source: Product owner)
- **Colours come from the Figma library’s “Colours” set: text is black at 80 / 60 / 40 / 20%.** Why: The app file binds its colours to a shared library with two sets of the same names; the newer “Colours” set (alpha black and white) is the one the revamped screens use. Primary text is black 80%, secondary 60%, placeholder 40%, disabled 20%; strokes are black 5 / 8 / 32%; the page is #FAFAFA and the dark surface #1F1F1F. (Source: Figma: 📱 EQAI Android · library “Colours”)
- **A colour at x% is the colour-guide colour at 100% with x% opacity.** Why: Figma paints the same brand and neutral colours at different opacities (green at 36% for unread strokes, lime at 8% for unread fills). Writing them as “{brand.green} @ 36%” keeps one source colour per hue, so a brand change flows to every tint. (Source: Product owner)
- **One-off greys snap to the text colours; readable text never drops below 4.5:1.** Why: Figma has about 20 hand-picked greys (#3C3C3C names, #858484 previews, #9F9F9F dates…). Snapping them to primary / secondary keeps new screens to four text colours. Black 40% is 2.85:1 on white, so it is only for placeholders and disabled text; dates and captions use secondary (60%, 5.7:1). Figma colours that fail AA for text are darkened in the same hue and the reason is written on the token. (Source: Product owner + accessibility)
- **Every colour token says what it is for and is used somewhere.** Why: Tokens that no Figma screen or component uses were deleted in the rebuild. The Colour page lists each token’s purpose and the components that use it, so an unused or duplicate colour is visible at once. (Source: Figma rebuild)
- **Green (lime in dark) only for what you can touch.** Why: If green also decorates, users can’t tell what is tappable. Reserving it for actions and the assistant’s byline makes every green thing a promise that it does something. (Source: Typography v3 colour roles)
- **In dark mode every green is lime (#BAFF29).** Why: Brand green goes muddy on near-black; lime is the brand’s dark-mode accent. Accents (buttons, icons, strokes, the FAB, the WhatsApp glyph) use lime itself, and green-tinted dark surfaces are re-hued to lime at the same darkness. Anything drawn on lime is dark (text/on-action), never white. (Source: Design rule)
- **Every text pair passes WCAG AA (4.5:1).** Why: Many users read the app outdoors on mid-range phones at low brightness. When a mock’s colour falls short (e.g. the saved-contact blue at 4.15:1), the token is nudged until it passes and the reason is written on the token. (Source: Accessibility)
- **Everything is set in DM Sans. Nothing is in Lora.** Why: One family keeps every screen consistent and the app light to ship. Some design files use Lora for display lines; in the product those lines are DM Sans. (Source: Product: “Make everything DM Sans”)
- **Four DM Sans weights: 400, 500, 600 and 700.** Why: Regular is for reading, Medium for labels, SemiBold where the designs use it (plan names such as “Equal AI Unlimited”), Bold for display lines. All four are loaded on web and Android, so nothing is synthesised. (Source: Design files)
- **Text that doesn’t match a type token is a bug.** Why: Twelve tokens cover every role. Ad-hoc sizes creep in one screen at a time until nothing lines up; holding to the tokens keeps rhythm across screens. (Source: Typography v3)
- **Medium is scanned, Regular is read; wrapping text is always Regular.** Why: Weight separates labels from prose. Paragraphs in Medium are tiring to read and flatten the hierarchy. (Source: Typography v3)
- **Emoji are sized to the label they sit in.** Why: Emoji render larger than letters at the same font size, so oversized emoji pull the eye away from the words. Matching the label size keeps chips calm. (Source: Design review: emoji looked too big)

entries.name: decisions/android-frame-chrome
entries.title: Android frame & chrome
entries.summary: - **Design at 390 × 800 dp and extend only vertically.** Why: It is the team’s working Android frame. Long screens grow taller rather than wider, so layouts are always checked at real phone width. (Source: Product: team frame) - **The status bar and every icon follow Material 3.*
entries.text:
## Android frame & chrome

- **Design at 390 × 800 dp and extend only vertically.** Why: It is the team’s working Android frame. Long screens grow taller rather than wider, so layouts are always checked at real phone width. (Source: Product: team frame)
- **The status bar and every icon follow Material 3.** Why: The app runs inside Android’s system UI. A Material 3 status bar (52 dp) and Material Symbols for all flat icons mean screens sit naturally next to the real system UI and every icon shares one line weight. (Source: Product: Material 3)
- **Text fields have 12 dp corners; search and assistant message fields are fully rounded.** Why: Form fields read as editable boxes. Search and the assistant composer are conversational entry points, so they use the pill shape the app uses for chat input. (Source: Design: text field 12px; assistant fields fully rounded)
- **48 dp touch targets, even when the visual is smaller.** Why: Smaller targets cause mis-taps, especially one-handed. Where a mock draws a 36 dp button, the touch area is still 48 dp. (Source: Accessibility / Material)
- **Business logic in Kotlin, UI in Compose, animations in Lottie.** Why: That is how the Android team builds. Components are stateless Compose; illustrative motion is Lottie JSON played by Lottie, never re-built by hand. (Source: Engineering: Android stack)
- **Respect reduced motion everywhere.** Why: Some users get motion sickness or find animation distracting. Every animation in the system holds still when the phone asks for reduced motion. (Source: Accessibility)

entries.title: People & identity
entries.summary: - **Free users get the plain avatar; paid users get the gold background and ring.** Why: Unlimited should feel like a status the user can see on their own face. Keeping free plain makes the upgrade visible without nagging. (Source: Product) - **Saved contacts show initials on a t
entries.text:
## People & identity

- **Free users get the plain avatar; paid users get the gold background and ring.** Why: Unlimited should feel like a status the user can see on their own face. Keeping free plain makes the upgrade visible without nagging. (Source: Product)
- **Saved contacts show initials on a tinted disc with a person badge.** Why: The badge is the signifier for “someone you know”. The disc colour varies per contact (blue, green, purple, orange, pink, teal) at the same saturation and lightness, so a list isn’t one flat colour, and every pair keeps the initials readable (AA). The same initials always get the same colour. (Source: Design: “AN with a mark”; colour can vary at the same saturation)
- **Unknown and business callers use 3D category art.** Why: The category tells the user at a glance why someone called (delivery, bank, real estate) before reading a word. (Source: Design)
- **The robot is the default “AI Assistant is On” art; the phone-with-sparkles is an experiment.** Why: Design confirmed the robot as final. The phone stays available as a prop so the team can test it. (Source: Product decision)
- **Green mascots are generated to order.** Why: Mascot moments are custom for each screen. When a new one is needed, the system shows a placeholder and asks for the art rather than reusing a mismatched pose. (Source: Design)
- **The logo comes from the official SVG.** Why: A traced logo drifts from the brand. The official vector generates both platforms (npm run logo). (Source: Brand)
- **In the AI layer, saved contacts are addressed by first name, others by full name.** Why: “Replying Amit” reads naturally for a friend, but splitting a business name gives nonsense like “Replying Dr.”. (Source: Engineering (copy))

entries.name: decisions/components
entries.title: Components
entries.summary: - **Build from atoms: atoms → molecules → organisms → screens.** Why: Every visible leaf (text, icon, emoji, image, coded art) is rendered by an atom (Text, Icon, Emoji, Asset, Button…). Molecules combine atoms for one job (a chip, a row), organisms are whole sections (a chat row
entries.text:
## Components

- **Build from atoms: atoms → molecules → organisms → screens.** Why: Every visible leaf (text, icon, emoji, image, coded art) is rendered by an atom (Text, Icon, Emoji, Asset, Button…). Molecules combine atoms for one job (a chip, a row), organisms are whole sections (a chat row, a paywall). Trace walks this chain, so a designer can point at any pixel and find the atom, then step up with ↑ to the molecule and section. (Source: Product owner)
- **Corner radii are whole numbers from one scale.** Why: The Figma scale is 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 18, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 50, 54, 80, 100 and full. Decimal radii in Figma (5.76, 1.33, 10.27…) come from scaled component instances or circles; use the whole number the master component uses, and “full” for circles and pills. (Source: Figma audit)
- **Action cards: grey body on a white card, never a green card.** Why: A green wrapper made confirmations look like warnings and broke consistency with the rest of the thread. Every action card has the same frame; the content says what happened. (Source: Design review)
- **Every action-card CTA has an emoji (📤 Send, ✏️ Edit, 👍 Confirm, 🗑️ Delete).** Why: Emoji make the action recognisable at a glance and match the chip language used everywhere else in chat. (Source: Design review)
- **All actions in a card have the same weight; Confirm is not a filled button.** Why: Two actions at equal weight let the user choose; a filled Confirm pushes them. The commit goes first, the revise second, both as text rows. (Source: Typography v3 / handoff)
- **Instructions use the note_stack icon with When / Do lines, never a category avatar.** Why: An instruction is a rule the user set, not a caller. The icon and When / Do structure make that obvious. (Source: Design review)
- **Flat icons are Material Symbols (Material 3); actions use emoji.** Why: One icon family keeps line weight consistent. Emoji on actions add warmth and are easier to recognise in a crowded chat. (Source: Design direction)
- **Premium (monetization) perk icons are filled, 16 dp, in the gold radial gradient.** Why: Filled gold marks a paid perk apart from everyday UI icons, which are outlined. (Source: Design spec)

entries.name: decisions/monetization
entries.title: Monetization
entries.summary: - **Unlimited is ₹249; with EQUAL25 it is ₹149.** Why: Today’s default, confirmed by product; price and coupon are experiment props (price, discountedPrice). The coupon row says “Save Flat ₹100”, and the price drop animates only when the user taps APPLY. (Source: Product decision
entries.text:
## Monetization

- **Unlimited is ₹249; with EQUAL25 it is ₹149.** Why: Today’s default, confirmed by product; price and coupon are experiment props (price, discountedPrice). The coupon row says “Save Flat ₹100”, and the price drop animates only when the user taps APPLY. (Source: Product decision)
- **The plan value card shows ₹39 with ₹49 struck through.** Why: The value designs show both orders; ₹39 / ₹49 was confirmed. (Source: Product decision)
- **🎊 LIMITED TIME DISCOUNT stays an emoji, not art.** Why: Confirmed by design: it is copy, not an illustration. (Source: Design decision)
- **Gold is only for subscription: paywall, plan, renewal, payment and anything else about Equal AI Unlimited.** Why: Gold means “premium”. Keeping it to subscription surfaces makes it a reliable signal and keeps the rest of the app green. Its white-on-gold contrast at the sheen is an accepted brand decision, like brand green. (Source: Product owner)
- **Every piece of text is DM Sans, including system mocks.** Why: One family everywhere. Even the mock status bar clock, the dialer stand-in and the call-handling device bar use DM Sans, not Roboto or the system font. (Source: Product owner)
- **Lock content, never identity.** Why: Free users still see who called and when; only the content (bubbles, recording, actions) is blurred or crown-locked. Hiding the caller would make the app useless, not tempting. (Source: Product)
- **While a payment is processing, every surface says so and the paywall button is disabled.** Why: UPI confirmations can take minutes. Without this, users who close the pending page pay twice. (Source: Design: If User Closes the payment pending page)
- **The exit offer appears once per session.** Why: Offering the coupon when someone leaves converts; offering it every time trains people to leave first. (Source: System guidance (not yet enforced in code))
- **Show what Unlimited did before asking for a renewal.** Why: A user who sees “20 calls handled” renews for the value they already got, not on a promise. (Source: Design: Monetization value)
- **Keep the existing bottom navigation (Chats, You).** Why: One mock showed a Home tab; product confirmed the navigation stays as it is. (Source: Product decision)

entries.name: decisions/assistant-calls
entries.title: Assistant & calls
entries.summary: - **The green orb opens the same assistant sheet on every screen.** Why: One consistent entry point means users learn it once. (Source: Design: Global MYA) - **Inside a chat, the task sheet stops below the chat header.** Why: The user must still see whose chat they are acting in,
entries.text:
## Assistant & calls

- **The green orb opens the same assistant sheet on every screen.** Why: One consistent entry point means users learn it once. (Source: Design: Global MYA)
- **Inside a chat, the task sheet stops below the chat header.** Why: The user must still see whose chat they are acting in, so a reply never goes to the wrong person. (Source: Design: chat AI layer)
- **Tasks end in a result the user confirms (Edit / Confirm), then the outcome shows where it lives.** Why: The assistant acts on the user’s behalf; confirming first keeps them in control, and showing the result in the chat row closes the loop. (Source: Design: Global MYA)
- **Confirm before actions that are hard to undo (mute, send, save).** Why: The assistant acts for the user. A one-line check (“Are you sure? You’ll not get any call from them…”) prevents the mistake that costs the most. (Source: Design: Mute, Reply on WhatsApp, Save Contact)
- **Every finished action leaves an action card in the chat.** Why: The chat is the record of what the assistant did (Outgoing call, Muted, WhatsApp message, Contact saved), and each card links to where the result lives. (Source: Design: action flows)
- **Hand off to the phone for the dialer, Settings and WhatsApp; never redraw them.** Why: The system owns those screens. The app hands off, then picks up where the user left off (“You stopped between saving this contact. Want to continue?”). (Source: Design: Call Back, Save Contact)
- **Errors say what happened in one line and offer one fix.** Why: Retry for a failed generation, Refresh or Try again when offline, “hold and speak again” for voice. One clear next step beats an error code. (Source: Design: Error states)
- **The contact form has two candidate designs (iOS-revamp parity, WhatsApp parity).** Why: The team hasn’t chosen; both are props on one form so either can ship. (Source: Design: Save Contact)
- **A missed call shows only what we know: the reason (with caller art and 👍/👎), else the name, else “Missed by the assistant”.** Why: Inventing a reason would mislead the call-back decision. The thumbs rate the reason, so they only appear with one. The warm tint says “missed”, not “error”. (Source: Design: missed-call card)
- **Never draw the system keyboard in the app.** Why: Android owns the keyboard. The docs show a stand-in image; the app only lifts its input above the keyboard. (Source: Engineering)
- **Ask for a permission only at the step that needs it, and say why in one line.** Why: Permissions asked up front get denied. Asked in context (“I need your contact list to know who is calling”), they get granted. (Source: Design: Known Calls flow)
- **Notifications: who, what they want, and Takeover first.** Why: A notification is glanced at in a second. Takeover is the action that matters most when the assistant is on a call with someone you know. (Source: Design: Notifications - Known Calls)
- **Silent Mode is titled “Silent Mode” everywhere.** Why: The dark mock said “Call Preferences”; design confirmed “Silent Mode” to match the You-tab row. (Source: Design decision)
- **Auto-rickshaw, paper bag and delivery rider are not caller categories.** Why: They appeared in a design as decoration; product confirmed they shouldn’t become categories. (Source: Product decision)

entries.name: action-chips
entries.title: Action chips
entries.summary: Emoji-led glass chips for the next step after a call: small chips in the chat list, large chips inside a conversation or the AI panel.
entries.text:
# Action chips (`action-chips`)
Group: Actions

Emoji-led glass chips for the next step after a call: small chips in the chat list, large chips inside a conversation or the AI panel.

- React: `import { SmallActionChip, LargeActionChip, ChipRow } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `SmallActionChip`, `LargeActionChip`
- Tokens: `gradient/chip-small-unread`, `gradient/chip-small-read`, `gradient/chip-large`, `action/stroke/unread`, `stroke/subtle`, `shadow/glass`, `text/action`, `text/secondary`, `text/primary`
- Source: §9 Small Action Chip · §10 Large Action Chip

Do: Lead every action with a Unicode emoji (📞 Call Back, ✏️ Update Address, 🗓️ Add to Calendar); actions use emoji, not Material icons. Use small chips outside chats (the chat list) and large chips inside a conversation or the AI panel. Let ChatListItem pick the small-chip state: unread rows get unread chips, read rows read chips, a selected row outlined chips. Mark the suggested next step unread and the alternative read (👍 Confirm vs ✍️ Edit).

Don't: Don't swap the emoji for a Material icon or drop it on some chips in a row. Don't wrap the chat-list chip row; it scrolls and clips at the right edge. Don't use a chip for a destructive action; that belongs in a confirm sheet.

Anatomy:
1. Container: Glass pill that holds the action and takes the tap. (Small 30 high, padding 8 start / 10 end · Large 40 high, padding 10 / 12 · radius full · 1dp action/stroke/unread (unread, large) or stroke/subtle (read) · gradient/chip-small-unread, gradient/chip-small-read or gradient/chip-large · shadow/glass on read and small unread · 48 touch target)
2. Emoji: Unicode emoji that leads every action (📞 Call back). (Emoji atom · Small 12 · Large 14 · gap 6 · platform emoji font · decorative)
3. Label: Sentence-case action name, one line. (Text atom · Small buttonSmall 12/500 · Large button 14/500 · small unread text/action, read / outlined text/secondary · large text/primary)
4. Chevron: Trailing arrow on small chips that signals it opens something. (chevron-right 14 · tint follows the label · gap 4 · always on in Compose, `chevron` prop on web (default on))
5. Small chip: locked: Free-plan variant where a crown-lock replaces the emoji and tapping opens the paywall. (crown-lock 14 Asset, alt / contentDescription 'Locked' · fill paywall/hero-top mixed 45% into bg/surface · 1dp paywall/card-stroke · label and chevron text/gold)
6. ChipRow: Horizontal scroller that holds a row of chips and clips at the right edge. (web only · gap 12 default · padding 2 top / 4 bottom · .eq-hscroll, scrollbar hidden · `wrap` to wrap instead)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Native <button>; the emoji and chevron are aria-hidden. Android: clickable(role = Role.Button) on the Row.
- Name. Web: The visible label; a locked chip reads 'Locked' (crown-lock alt) followed by the label. Android: Merged text of the chip; EmojiGlyph is cleared from semantics, so only the label is read, with 'Locked' first on a locked chip.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to each chip, Enter or Space to activate; ChipRow scrolls horizontally as focus moves. Focus draws shadow/focusRing. Android: TalkBack: swipe through chips in order, double-tap to activate; the row scrolls to the focused chip. No visible hardware-keyboard focus indicator.
- Touch target. Web: Both chips use .eq-touch, so the 30px and 40px pills get a 48px hit area. Android: minimumInteractiveComponentSize() on both, so the 30dp and 40dp pills get a 48dp target.
- Contrast. Web: Small unread label text/action #00B140 on gradient/chip-small-unread is about 2.7:1 in light (accepted brand green); read and outlined text/secondary 5.6:1, large text/primary 12.2:1, locked text/gold 4.4:1. Dark lime on the lime-tinted fill is 8.2:1. Android: Same tokens as web; the 1dp action/stroke/unread border is decorative, the label carries the meaning.
- State. Web: unread / read / outlined are visual emphasis only (colour and fill), with no ARIA state; the row's unread count and selection carry the real state. LargeActionChip disabled has no style of its own outside the Meet Your Assistant card. Android: Style is not exposed in semantics. LargeActionChip enabled = false sets disabled semantics and draws at 45%.
- Motion. Web: Press scale 0.97 over 120ms via .eq-pressable; zeroed under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: eqPressFeedback scale tween follows the system animator scale.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Accepted brand decision: ActionChip.css / ActionChips.kt small unread label text/action #00B140 on gradient/chip-small-unread is about 2.7:1 in light mode, below 4.5:1.
- ActionChip.css: LargeActionChip has no :disabled style (only .eq-mya-chips in Assistant.css dims it), while Compose dims to 45% when enabled = false.
- ActionChips.kt: both chips use indication = null with no focus ring, so hardware-keyboard focus is invisible.

Example: Small chip states
```tsx
<SmallActionChip emoji="📞" label="Call Back" />
<SmallActionChip emoji="✏️" label="Update Address" />
<SmallActionChip emoji="📞" label="Call Back" state="read" />
<SmallActionChip emoji="📞" label="Call Back" state="outlined" />
<SmallActionChip emoji="🗓️" label="Add to Calendar" state="outlined" chevron={false} />
```
```kotlin
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp)) {
    Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)) {
        SmallActionChip(label = "Call Back", emoji = "📞", onClick = {})
        SmallActionChip(label = "Update Address", emoji = "✏️", onClick = {})
    }
    SmallActionChip(label = "Call Back", emoji = "📞", onClick = {}, style = SmallActionChipStyle.Read)
    SmallActionChip(label = "Call Back", emoji = "📞", onClick = {}, style = SmallActionChipStyle.Outlined)
    // Compose: no chevron toggle; the trailing chevron is always shown.
    SmallActionChip(label = "Add to Calendar", emoji = "🗓️", onClick = {}, style = SmallActionChipStyle.Outlined)
}
```

Example: Large chips
```tsx
<ChipRow gap={8}>
  <LargeActionChip emoji="📞" label="Takeover" />
  <LargeActionChip emoji="🗓️" label="Ask to reschedule" />
</ChipRow>
<ChipRow gap={8}>
  <LargeActionChip emoji="✍️" label="Edit" state="read" />
  <LargeActionChip emoji="👍" label="Confirm" />
</ChipRow>
```
```kotlin
// Compose: no ChipRow; a Row with spacedBy(8.dp) does the same job.
Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)) {
    LargeActionChip(label = "Takeover", emoji = "📞", onClick = {})
    LargeActionChip(label = "Ask to reschedule", emoji = "🗓️", onClick = {})
}
Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)) {
    LargeActionChip(label = "Edit", emoji = "✍️", onClick = {}, state = LargeActionChipState.Read)
    LargeActionChip(label = "Confirm", emoji = "👍", onClick = {})
}
```

Example: In a chat row
```tsx
<ChipRow>
  <SmallActionChip emoji="📞" label="Call Back" />
  <SmallActionChip emoji="✏️" label="Update Address" />
  <SmallActionChip emoji="🗓️" label="Add to Calendar" />
</ChipRow>
```
```kotlin
// Compose: no ChipRow; a horizontally scrolling Row (gap 12) clips at the right edge.
Row(
    modifier = Modifier.horizontalScroll(rememberScrollState()),
    horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp),
) {
    SmallActionChip(label = "Call Back", emoji = "📞", onClick = {})
    SmallActionChip(label = "Update Address", emoji = "✏️", onClick = {})
    SmallActionChip(label = "Add to Calendar", emoji = "🗓️", onClick = {})
}
```

entries.name: button
entries.title: Button
entries.summary: Filled, text and icon buttons: use a filled Button for the one commit action on a surface, a TextButton for revise or secondary actions, and an IconButton for icon-only controls like back, close and call.
entries.text:
# Button (`button`)
Group: Actions

Filled, text and icon buttons: use a filled Button for the one commit action on a surface, a TextButton for revise or secondary actions, and an IconButton for icon-only controls like back, close and call.

- React: `import { Button, TextButton, IconButton } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `EqualButton`, `EqualTextButton`, `EqualIconButton`
- Tokens: `button/primary`, `button/secondary`, `button/danger`, `button/disabled`, `text/on-action`, `text/on-danger`, `text/on-action-disabled`, `text/action`, `text/danger`, `bg/surface`, `shadow/raised`, `glass-button/default`, `shadow/focusRing`
- Source: §19 Buttons

Do: Use exactly one filled Button per surface for the commit action (Save, Delete, Turn off); pair it with a TextButton for revise or cancel. Write labels in sentence case ("Add new Address", "Share Feedback" as shipped) and keep the same verb from control to confirmation: Turn off → "Call learning turned off". Use the danger variant only for destructive commits, with the trash icon (the delete sheet does this for you). Always pass a `label` to IconButton; it is the accessible name and the tooltip.

Don't: Don't put two filled buttons side by side; two actions at equal weight are one action. Don't colour non-actionable text green; text/action is reserved for things you can tap. Don't shrink the touch target: small buttons keep a 48dp hit area even when the visual is 24dp.

Anatomy:
1. Container: The pill (or 8dp rounded) surface that holds the content and takes the press. (sm 24 · md 36 · lg 45 high · radius full (rounded: radius/sm 8) · fill button/primary, button/secondary, button/danger, gradient/cta-gold, or bg/surface / transparent + 1.5 inset border (text/gold, button/primary) · disabled button/disabled · 48 touch target)
2. Leading icon: Optional icon before the label that reinforces the action. (Icon atom · web 18 (sm 14) · Compose 16 · gap 6 (web sm 4) · tint follows the label colour · decorative)
3. Label: The verb that names the action, sentence case, one line. (Text atom · button 14/500 (sm buttonSmall 12/500; Gold Bold) · text/on-action, text/on-secondary, text/on-danger, white (Gold), text/action (Outline), text/gold (GoldOutline) · padding h14 / h20 / h24)
4. Trailing icon: Optional icon after the label, usually a chevron for forward navigation. (Same size and tint as the leading icon · gap 6)
5. TextButton: label: Unfilled text action used for the revise or secondary action. (button 14/500 (web small buttonSmall 12/500) · text/action, text/danger or text/secondary (web neutral) · web min height 20, Compose 36 high, padding h8 · icons 18 / 16 · disabled text/action-disabled)
6. IconButton: circle + icon: Icon-only circular button for close, confirm and toolbar actions. (web ghost / danger-ghost 40, icon 24 · neutral 44 bg/surface + shadow/raised, icon text/secondary · glass 44 glass-button/default + shadow/glass, icon text/primary · primary 42 button/primary, icon text/on-action · filled icons 22)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Native <button type='button'> for Button, TextButton and IconButton. Android: clickable(role = Role.Button) on the Row/Box; the icons inside have contentDescription = null except the IconButton glyph.
- Name. Web: Button and TextButton take their name from the visible label; IconButton requires `label`, set as aria-label and title. Android: Name comes from the text; EqualIconButton takes a contentDescription (pass a verb such as 'Close').
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to focus, Enter or Space to activate; disabled buttons leave the tab order. Focus draws shadow/focusRing via .eq-reset-btn:focus-visible. Android: TalkBack: swipe to focus, double-tap to activate. EqualButton draws eqFocusRing on hardware-keyboard focus; EqualTextButton and EqualIconButton draw no focus indicator.
- Touch target. Web: Every Button, TextButton and IconButton carries .eq-touch, a 48px ::after hit area around the 24 / 36 / 45px pill, the 20px text action and the 40–44px circles. Android: minimumInteractiveComponentSize() on all three, so sm 24, md 36, lg 45, TextButton 36 and the 42 / 44 circles get a 48dp target.
- Contrast. Web: White on button/primary #00B140 is 2.85:1 in light (accepted brand green). Secondary text/on-secondary on lime 11.2:1, danger white on #C50000 6.2:1, GoldOutline text/gold 4.6:1; the Gold white label on gradient/cta-gold falls to 2.3:1 at its #C8A774 stop. Dark black on lime is 17.4:1. Android: Same tokens and ratios as web; TextButton and Outline text/action #00B140 on white are 2.85:1 in light, lime on #1F1F1F is 13.7:1 in dark.
- State. Web: Disabled uses the native disabled attribute and swaps to button/disabled with text/on-action-disabled; TextButton turns text/action-disabled; IconButton drops to 40% opacity. Android: enabled = false on clickable marks the node disabled; EqualButton swaps to button/disabled and TextButton to text/action-disabled, but Neutral and Glass EqualIconButtons keep their look.
- Motion. Web: Press scales to 0.97 over 120ms and the fill fades over 200ms; the Gold sheen and glow loop stop and base.css zeroes durations under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: eqPressFeedback tweens the scale over motion.fast and follows the system animator scale; the Gold sheen and glow are skipped when rememberReduceMotion() is true.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Accepted brand decision: Button.css / Buttons.kt white label on button/primary #00B140 is 2.85:1 in light mode, below 4.5:1 for 14sp text.
- Accepted brand decision: Button.css / Buttons.kt TextButton tone 'action' and the Outline variant (text/action #00B140 on white) are 2.85:1 in light mode.
- Accepted brand decision (premium gold, subscription surfaces only): button.css / Buttons.kt: the Gold variant's white label on gradient/cta-gold drops to 2.3:1 at the #C8A774 stop (4.2:1 at #A37236), below 4.5:1.
- Buttons.kt: EqualTextButton and EqualIconButton use indication = null with no eqFocusRing, so hardware-keyboard focus is invisible (only EqualButton draws a ring).
- Buttons.kt: EqualIconButton Neutral and Glass ignore enabled = false visually (same fill and tint), while web dims IconButton to 40%.

Example: Variants
```tsx
<Button>Save</Button>
<Button variant="secondary">Try Voices</Button>
<Button variant="danger" leadingIcon="delete">Delete</Button>
<Button disabled>Save</Button>
```
```kotlin
EqualButton(text = "Save", onClick = {})
EqualButton(text = "Try Voices", onClick = {}, variant = EqualButtonVariant.Secondary)
EqualButton(text = "Delete", onClick = {}, variant = EqualButtonVariant.Danger, leadingIcon = EqualIcons.Delete)
EqualButton(text = "Save", onClick = {}, enabled = false)
```

Example: Sizes
```tsx
<Button size="sm" leadingIcon="add">Apply</Button>
<Button size="md">Save</Button>
<Button size="lg">Save</Button>
<Button shape="rounded">Save</Button>

<Button block size="lg" leadingIcon="add">Add New Instruction</Button>
```
```kotlin
EqualButton(text = "Apply", onClick = {}, size = EqualButtonSize.Sm, leadingIcon = EqualIcons.Add)
EqualButton(text = "Save", onClick = {}, size = EqualButtonSize.Md)
EqualButton(text = "Save", onClick = {}, size = EqualButtonSize.Lg)
// Block = lg metrics at full width
EqualButton(text = "Add New Instruction", onClick = {}, size = EqualButtonSize.Block, leadingIcon = EqualIcons.Add)
```

Example: Text and icon buttons
```tsx
<TextButton>Edit</TextButton>
<TextButton leadingIcon="share">Share</TextButton>
<TextButton trailingIcon="chevron-right">Share Feedback</TextButton>
<TextButton tone="neutral">Cancel</TextButton>
<TextButton tone="danger">Delete address</TextButton>
<TextButton size="small">Clear all</TextButton>

<IconButton icon="arrow-back" label="Back" />
<IconButton icon="delete" label="Delete" variant="danger-ghost" />
<IconButton icon="close" label="Close" variant="neutral" />
<IconButton icon="check" label="Confirm" variant="primary" />
```
```kotlin
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)) {
    EqualTextButton(text = "Edit", onClick = {})
    EqualTextButton(text = "Share", onClick = {}, leadingIcon = EqualIcons.Share)
    EqualTextButton(text = "Share Feedback", onClick = {}, trailingIcon = EqualIcons.ChevronRight)
    EqualTextButton(text = "Delete address", onClick = {}, danger = true)
}
Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)) {
    EqualIconButton(icon = EqualIcons.Back, contentDescription = "Back", onClick = {})
    EqualIconButton(icon = EqualIcons.Check, contentDescription = "Confirm", onClick = {}, variant = EqualIconButtonVariant.Primary)
}
```

Example: Commit + revise
```tsx
<TextButton tone="neutral">Cancel</TextButton>
<Button>Turn off</Button>
```
```kotlin
Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)) {
    EqualTextButton(text = "Cancel", onClick = {})
    EqualButton(text = "Turn off", onClick = {})
}
```

entries.name: assistant-sheet
entries.title: Assistant sheet (Global MYA)
entries.summary: The sheet the green orb opens on any screen: greeting, quick-action tiles, suggestion chips and a text or voice input. A request turns it into a short task conversation (voice note → Thinking… → result card → Edit / Confirm).
entries.text:
# Assistant sheet (Global MYA) (`assistant-sheet`)
Group: Assistant

The sheet the green orb opens on any screen: greeting, quick-action tiles, suggestion chips and a text or voice input. A request turns it into a short task conversation (voice note → Thinking… → result card → Edit / Confirm).

- React: `import { AssistantSheetShell, AssistantGreeting, AssistantActions, AssistantInput, VoiceRecorder, TrySaying, AssistantTaskHeader, AssistantThinking, AssistantReplies, CarouselDots } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `AssistantSheetShell`, `AssistantGreeting`, `AssistantActions`, `AssistantInput`, `VoiceRecorder`, `TrySaying`, `AssistantTaskHeader`, `AssistantThinking`, `AssistantReplies`, `CarouselDots`
- Tokens: `bg/primary`, `gradient/voice-note`, `text/action`, `action/stroke/unread`, `text/danger`, `component/chat/wallpaper-bg`
- Source: Global MYA

Props of `AssistantInput`:
- `mode`: `'text' | 'voice'`. Field + mic, or keyboard toggle + Send voice note.
- `value?`: `string` = ''. Text.
- `focused?`: `boolean`. Green outline (keyboard open).
- `onMic?`: `() => void`. Text → voice.
- `onKeyboard?`: `() => void`. Voice → text.
- `onVoiceNote?`: `() => void`. Tap to record.
- `onVoiceHold?`: `() => void`. Press and hold to record.
- `onSubmit?`: `(text: string) => void`. Send.

Props of `VoiceRecorder`:
- `state`: `'idle' | 'recording' | 'hold' | 'cancel'`. Bar state.
- `seconds?`: `number` = 0. Elapsed.
- `onDelete?`: `() => void`. Discard.
- `onSend?`: `() => void`. Send.

Props of `AssistantGreeting`:
- `name`: `string`. First name, in text/action.
- `greeting?`: `string` = 'Good morning'. Use greetingFor(hour).

Props of `AssistantActions`:
- `items`: `{ label; icon: IconName | 'equal'; onClick? }[]`. Three tiles.

Props of `AssistantSheetShell`:
- `task?`: `boolean`. The taller conversation sheet (wallpaper body).
- `header?`: `ReactNode`. AssistantTaskHeader in task mode.
- `footer?`: `ReactNode`. Input / recorder.
- `onScrim?`: `() => void`. Tap outside closes.

Do: Open it from the green orb on every screen; it is the same sheet everywhere. Title the task by what the assistant is doing, not what the user said. End with a result to confirm (Edit / Confirm), then close and show the outcome where it lives (the chat row).

Don't: Don't draw the keyboard; it's the system's. Only lift the input above it. Don't keep the tiles while typing; the keyboard needs the room.

Anatomy:
1. Sheet: AssistantSheetShell: the panel the green orb opens over a dimmed screen. (bg/primary · radius 32 top · shadow 0 -8 30 black 12% · task: 82% height, chat/wallpaper-bg body · inChat: stops 112 below the top · footer padding 12/16/20)
2. AssistantGreeting: Orb, greeting with the user's name and the prompt. (56 orb (decorative) · headline Bold, name in text/action · prompt body1 text/secondary · padding 24/24/0 · gap 2)
3. AssistantActions: Three quick-action tiles. (3 equal columns, gap 10 · min 92 high · radius 16 · bg/surface · shadow 0 2 8 black 6% · icon 30 text/action (or Equal mark) · label body2 Regular)
4. AssistantInput: Text field with mic/send, or the voice row. (text: 48 pill, bg/surface, 1dp stroke/subtle (focus 1.5dp button/primary), bodyLarge, placeholder text/placeholder + 52 circle gradient/voice-note · voice: 48 keyboard circle + 52 'Send voice note' pill, subheading Bold text/on-action)
5. VoiceRecorder: Recording bar with delete, timer, RecordingWaveform and send. (48 delete text/danger · 48 pill, 1.5dp action/stroke/unread, padding 0 18, m:ss body1 tabular + 22 bars (3 wide, gap 2) text/action (cancel text/danger) · 52 send · hold/cancel hint caption Regular text/secondary)
6. AssistantTaskHeader: Header once a request becomes a task. (32 orb · title subheading Regular · neutral close (40 web with 48 touch / EqualIconButton 44 in 48) · bg/surface raised)
7. AssistantThinking: The assistant working. (28 orb · 'Thinking…' subheading italic text/secondary · dots pulse 1.2s, staggered 0.2s)
8. AssistantReplies + CarouselDots: Edit / Confirm pills under a result, and page dots. (48 pills, gap 12 · emoji + subheading Regular · Edit bg/surface + 1dp stroke/subtle · Confirm gradient/chip-large + action/stroke/unread · dots 7 (active 11), gap 8, stroke/medium / action/stroke/unread)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Panel is role=dialog 'Your assistant' (aria-modal in overlay); greeting is h2; tiles, mic, send and replies are buttons; the field is in a form; recorder pill is role=timer; the hold hint and Thinking are role=status; CarouselDots is role=img. Android: Panel sets paneTitle 'Your assistant'; tiles, circles and pills are clickable(Role.Button); the voice pill is combinedClickable; Thinking merges with liveRegion Polite; the hold hint is a polite live region; dots are cleared to one description.
- Name. Web: Field 'Message your assistant'; buttons 'Voice note', 'Send', 'Type instead', 'Delete recording', 'Send voice note', 'Close'. Orbs are decorative (label ''). Android: Same labels via contentDescription / onClickLabel; long-press label 'Hold to record'; greeting reads '{greeting}, {name}'; orbs have no description; dots 'Card 1 of 3'.
- Keyboard. Web: useModal moves focus in, traps Tab and closes on Escape (onClose, else onScrim). Tab through tiles, field (Enter submits), mic/send. Hold-to-record is pointer-only; Enter or Space on Send voice note records with a tap. Android: TalkBack: double-tap to activate; double-tap and hold triggers Hold to record; the IME Send key submits. System Back calls onScrim.
- Touch target. Web: Mic/send 52, round buttons 48, replies 48, reply-card actions min 48, tiles 92+, task close 40 with eq-touch (48). Android: Voice circles use minimumInteractiveComponentSize; round buttons and pills are 48dp; close is EqualIconButton (48).
- Contrast. Web: Accepted brand decision: white icons and label on gradient/voice-note run 1.5:1 at the lime end to 2.85:1 at green; the name, tile icons and reply-card actions in text/action are 2.6–2.85:1 in light. Placeholder text/placeholder is 2.85:1. Dark is black on lime, 17:1. TrySaying text/secondary is 5.7:1 on bg/primary. Android: Same tokens and ratios as web.
- State. Web: Recording is shown with a timer and text ('Release to send, slide left to cancel', 'Release to cancel') announced through role=status, plus a red waveform on cancel. Focus shows the green outline. Android: Same text; the hold/cancel hint is a polite live region and the timer reads 'Recording 0:04'.
- Motion. Web: Sheet slides up, waveform ticks every 120ms, Thinking dots pulse. Under prefers-reduced-motion the bars stop and the dots and slide are removed. Android: rememberReduceMotion stops the bars and dots and shows the sheet without the slide.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Hold-to-record (onVoiceHold) in Assistant.tsx is pointer-only (onPointerDown timer); keyboard users can only tap to record.
- Accepted brand decision: white icons and 'Send voice note' on gradient/voice-note are 1.5–2.85:1, and text/action on light surfaces (greeting name, tile icons, reply-card actions) 2.6–2.85:1, in light theme (Assistant.tsx/.css and Assistant.kt).
- The message field placeholder (text/placeholder, Assistant.css .eq-mya-field::placeholder and Assistant.kt) is 2.85:1 on bg/surface, below 4.5:1.

Example: Greeting & quick actions
```tsx
<AssistantSheetShell footer={<AssistantInput mode="text" onMic={toVoice} onSubmit={send} />} onScrim={close}>
  <AssistantGreeting name="Keshav" />
  <AssistantActions items={quickActions} />
  <ChipRow><LargeActionChip emoji="🗓️" label="Reply Amit on WhatsApp" /> …</ChipRow>
</AssistantSheetShell>
```
```kotlin
EqualTheme {
    AssistantSheetShell(
        onScrim = { /* close */ },
        footer = { AssistantInput(mode = AssistantInputMode.Text, onMic = { /* to voice */ }, onSubmit = { /* send */ }) },
    ) {
        AssistantGreeting(name = "Keshav")
        AssistantActions(
            items = listOf(
                AssistantAction("Talk to Equal"), // null icon: the Equal mark
                AssistantAction("Talk to Equal", EqualIcons.AutoFix),
                AssistantAction("Make a call", EqualIcons.CallFilled),
            ),
        )
        AssistantChips {
            LargeActionChip(label = "Reply Amit on WhatsApp", emoji = "\uD83D\uDDD3\uFE0F", onClick = {})
            LargeActionChip(label = "Set reminder", emoji = "\uD83D\uDD14", onClick = {})
        }
    }
}
```

Example: Input: text and voice
```tsx
<AssistantInput mode="text" value={text} onChange={setText} onMic={() => setMode('voice')} onSubmit={send} />
<AssistantInput mode="voice" onKeyboard={() => setMode('text')} onVoiceNote={record} onVoiceHold={holdToRecord} />
```
```kotlin
EqualTheme {
    var mode by remember { mutableStateOf(AssistantInputMode.Text) }
    var text by remember { mutableStateOf("") }
    AssistantInput(
        mode = mode,
        value = text,
        onValueChange = { text = it },
        onMic = { mode = AssistantInputMode.Voice },
        onKeyboard = { mode = AssistantInputMode.Text },
        onSubmit = { /* send it */ },
        onVoiceNote = { /* record */ },
        onVoiceHold = { /* hold to record */ },
        modifier = Modifier.imePadding(), // lift above the system keyboard
    )
}
```

Example: Recorder states
```tsx
<VoiceRecorder state="idle" onDelete={discard} onSend={send} />
<VoiceRecorder state="recording" seconds={elapsed} onDelete={discard} onSend={send} />
<VoiceRecorder state="hold" />    // press and hold: release to send, slide left to cancel
<VoiceRecorder state="cancel" />  // slid left: release to cancel
```
```kotlin
EqualTheme {
```

entries.title: Chat actions
entries.summary: What the AI layer uses to carry out a task in a chat and to fail well: the assistant’s turn, Hold to speak, the edit-in-place bubble, the new contact form (two parity options), the permission dialog and the offline sheet and screen.
entries.text:
# Chat actions (`chat-actions`)
Group: Assistant

What the AI layer uses to carry out a task in a chat and to fail well: the assistant’s turn, Hold to speak, the edit-in-place bubble, the new contact form (two parity options), the permission dialog and the offline sheet and screen.

- React: `import { AiTurn, HoldToSpeakBar, EditBubble, NewContactForm, PermissionDialog, OfflineSheet, OfflineScreen } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `AiTurn`, `HoldToSpeakBar`, `EditBubble`, `NewContactForm`, `PermissionDialog`, `OfflineSheet`, `OfflineScreen`, `DialerStandIn`
- Tokens: `button/primary`, `bg/surface`, `chat/wallpaper-bg`, `action/stroke/unread`
- Source: Flows/Call Back · Mute · Reply On WhatsApp · Save Contact · Error states

Props of `NewContactForm`:
- `value`: `{ first; last?; phone; email?; sync? }`. Pre-filled from the call.
- `variant?`: `'grouped' | 'outlined'` = 'grouped'. iOS-revamp parity or exact WhatsApp parity.
- `onSave?`: `() => void`. Save.

Props of `EditBubble`:
- `value`: `string`. The draft.
- `onChange?`: `(v: string) => void`. Typing.
- `onDone?`: `() => void`. Green check.

Props of `AiTurn`:
- `children`: `ReactNode`. What the assistant says.
- `actions?`: `{ label; emoji; onClick? }[]`. Action rows, emoji first.

Do: Confirm before anything the user can’t easily undo (mute, send, save). Leave the result in the chat as an action card, so the chat is the record of what the assistant did. On failure, say what happened in one line and offer the one action that fixes it.

Don't: Don't draw the dialer, Settings or WhatsApp; they belong to the phone. Hand off and show the result when the user comes back. Don't lose the user’s place: after Settings, offer to continue where they stopped.

Anatomy:
1. AiTurn: The assistant's turn: orb and reply card. (28 orb · gap 8 · AssistantReplyCard 280 wide, radius 16, bg/surface · sender body2 text/action · body1 · time micro text/secondary · min-48 emoji + label rows in text/action)
2. HoldToSpeakBar: Voice-first input with a keyboard toggle. (52 pill bg/surface, 1dp action/stroke/unread · mic 20 + button label text/primary · 48 keyboard circle bg/surface, icon 22 text/secondary)
3. EditBubble: Edit a draft in place above the keyboard. (padding 8/12 · gap 8 · textarea radius 20, padding 12/16, bodyLarge, bg/surface, grows to 300 · 48 button/primary Done circle with check 24 text/on-action)
4. NewContactForm: New contact form in two parity variants. (header: close, 'New contact' title Medium, sm Save (48 touch) · grouped: radius 16 groups on bg/primary · outlined: bg/surface, 48 fields, radius 8, 1dp stroke/dark (focus button/primary), floating 12 label text/secondary · Sync Switch)
5. PermissionDialog: Centred permission ask over a dimmed chat. (black 45% scrim · card radius 24, padding 24/16/16, bg/surface · 36 neutral close (48 touch) · 84 art · title Medium · body1 text/secondary · block lg CTA)
6. OfflineSheet / OfflineScreen: No-internet sheet over a chat, and the full screen. (sheet radius 28 top bg/surface, 64 art, title Medium, body2 Regular text/secondary, block lg Refresh · screen chat/wallpaper-bg, 120 art, Try again pinned at the bottom)
7. DialerStandIn: Coded stand-in for the phone's dialer in docs. (dark #1F2125 surface · 40/48 number · 60 keys · 128 × 56 #EE675C end button)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Buttons for Hold to speak, Type instead, Done, Save, Close and action rows; EditBubble is a textarea; outlined fields are inputs inside <label>; Sync is a Switch; PermissionDialog is role=dialog; OfflineSheet is role=alertdialog; DialerStandIn is role=group. Android: Role.Button on actions; BasicTextField fields with contentDescription; PermissionDialog and OfflineSheet set paneTitle with heading() titles; DialerStandIn has contentDescription 'Calling …'.
- Name. Web: 'Edit message', 'Done', 'Type instead', 'Close', 'Sync contact to phone', 'Calling {number}', 'End call'; outlined fields named by their label text; grouped values are plain text, not fields. The AiTurn orb is announced as 'Equal AI'. Android: Same strings; outlined field labels are cleared and repeated as the field's contentDescription; the AiTurn orb has no description.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab through fields and buttons; Hold to speak works with Enter/Space as a tap. PermissionDialog and OfflineSheet use useModal: focus moves in, Tab is trapped, Escape and the scrim call onClose. Android: TalkBack: double-tap Hold to speak; edit fields with the IME. System Back closes PermissionDialog (onClose) and OfflineSheet (onDismiss) when set.
- Touch target. Web: Done and keyboard circle 48; dialog close 36 with eq-touch (48); Save sm 24 with eq-touch (48); lg Buttons 45 with eq-touch (48). Android: Done and keyboard 48dp; SmallCloseButton has a 48dp box; EqualButton 48dp minimum.
- Contrast. Web: Accepted brand decision: the Done check and Save / Refresh / Try again labels are white on green, and reply-card actions text/action on white, 2.85:1 in light. Body text/secondary 5.7:1; field borders stroke/dark. Dark is lime with black content. Android: Same tokens and ratios as web.
- State. Web: Switch exposes checked; focused fields get the green border (the caret also shows). Offline is said in text. Android: Switch toggleable state; focus border as on web.
- Motion. Web: PermissionDialog pops in (couponSpring) and OfflineSheet slides up; both stop under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: Both start visible under rememberReduceMotion.

Known accessibility gaps:
- AiTurn in ChatActions.tsx renders AiAvatar without label='', so screen readers hear 'Equal AI' for the orb and again for the card's sender line (ChatActions.kt hides the orb).
- Accepted brand decision: EditBubble Done (white check on button/primary), the primary Save / Refresh / Try again buttons and text/action reply-card actions are 2.85:1 in light theme (ChatActions.tsx/.css and ChatActions.kt).

Example: Assistant turn
```tsx
<AiTurn actions={[{ label: 'Mute', emoji: '🔕', onClick: mute }]}>Are you sure? …</AiTurn>
```
```kotlin
EqualTheme {
    AiTurn(
        text = "Are you sure? You’ll not get any call from them even if it’s important",
        actions = listOf(ReplyAction(label = "Mute", emoji = "🔕", onClick = { /* mute */ })),
    )
}
```

Example: Hold to speak
```tsx
<HoldToSpeakBar onHold={record} onKeyboard={showKeyboard} />
```
```kotlin
EqualTheme {
    HoldToSpeakBar(onHold = { /* record */ }, onKeyboard = { /* show keyboard */ })
}
```

Example: Edit bubble
```tsx
<EditBubble value={draft} onChange={setDraft} onDone={save} autoFocus />
```
```kotlin
EqualTheme {
    var draft by remember { mutableStateOf("Hi Amit! Count me in for Sunday 8 PM. See you there 👍") }
    // Over the chat dimmed with EditDimColor; lift above the keyboard with imePadding()
    Box(Modifier.background(EditDimColor)) {
        EditBubble(value = draft, onValueChange = { draft = it }, onDone = { /* save */ }, autoFocus = true)
    }
}
```

Example: New contact: iOS parity
```tsx
<NewContactForm variant="grouped" value={contact} onClose={close} onSave={save} />
```
```kotlin

    NewContactForm(
        value = NewContactValue(first = "Rahul (Electrician)", phone = "+91 98717 46113"),
        variant = NewContactVariant.Grouped,
        onClose = { /* close */ },
        onSave = { /* save */ },
    )
}
```

Example: New contact: WhatsApp parity
```tsx
<NewContactForm variant="outlined" value={contact} onSave={save} onSync={setSync} />
```
```kotlin
EqualTheme {
    var sync by remember { mutableStateOf(true) }
    NewContactForm(
        value = NewContactValue(first = "Rahul (Electrician)", phone = "+91 98717 46113", sync = sync),
        variant = NewContactVariant.Outlined,
        onSave = { /* save */ },
        onSync = { sync = it },
    )
}
```

Example: Offline
```tsx
<OfflineSheet onRefresh={refresh} />   // over a chat
<OfflineScreen onRetry={retry} />    // nothing to show yet
```
```kotlin
EqualTheme {
    OfflineSheet(onRefresh = { /* refresh */ })   // over a chat
    OfflineScreen(onRetry = { /* retry */ })      // nothing to show yet
}
```

entries.name: action-card
entries.title: Action card
entries.summary: A card for something the assistant did or proposes (a WhatsApp reply, an appointment, a saved rule), with stacked actions underneath.
entries.text:
# Action card (`action-card`)
Group: Cards

A card for something the assistant did or proposes (a WhatsApp reply, an appointment, a saved rule), with stacked actions underneath.

- React: `import { ActionCard, ActionCardBody, instructionLines } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `ActionCard`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `bg/primary`, `stroke/subtle`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`, `text/action`, `button/primary`
- Source: §14 Action Card

Do: Put the positive action first (Confirm, Send), then the revise (Edit). Both are text rows. Name the source in the title ("WhatsApp · Amit Nanda") so the user knows where the action goes. Lead every action with its emoji (📤 Send, ✏️ Edit, 👍 Confirm, 🗑️ Delete).

Don't: Don't use a filled button inside an action card, not even for Confirm. Don't use a 3D category avatar for an instruction; use the note_stack icon with When / Do lines. Don't put the card on a green card; the grey body always sits on a white card. Don't use flat icons in action labels; the rows are emoji + text.

Anatomy:
1. Card: White card that frames the body and actions. (width 268 · bg/surface · radius lg (16) · overflow hidden · padding 8 around the body)
2. Body: Grey quote block (ActionCardBody, also used by the instruction preview). (bg/primary · radius md (12) · padding 8 · gap 12)
3. Source circle: Category avatar, Material icon or WhatsApp logo. (40 circle · bg/surface · CategoryAvatar 40 · Icon 22 text/action · whatsapp Icon 22 brand/whatsapp · web also takes any Asset (22))
4. Title: Where the action goes. (Text body2 · text/primary)
5. Quote / details: The quoted message or detail lines (When / Do for instructions). (Text body1 · text/secondary (When line text/primary))
6. Timestamp: When it happened. (Text micro · text/secondary · right-aligned · 2 above)
7. Action rows: Full-width emoji + label actions under dividers. (min height 44 (web TextButton) / 48 dp (Compose) · divider stroke/subtle · Emoji 14 · gap 6 · Text button text/action (danger text/danger))

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Each action is a <button> (TextButton); the body is text. Android: Each row is clickable(role = Role.Button); the body is text.
- Name. Web: Actions are named by their label; the emoji is aria-hidden; the WhatsApp logo is role=img "WhatsApp"; the category avatar reads its category name; a Material icon is hidden. Android: Rows read the label (EmojiGlyph is hidden); the WhatsApp icon reads "WhatsApp"; a Material icon has null contentDescription; the category avatar reads its label.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to each action; Enter / Space activates. Android: TalkBack: swipe to each row, double-tap.
- Touch target. Web: Rows are 44 px high and full width with eq-touch; stacked rows overlap their 48 px areas, and the last row's is clipped by the card. Android: Rows are 48 dp high and full width.
- Contrast. Web: Body text/secondary 5.7:1 and title text/primary 12.3:1 on bg/primary. Action labels and the instruction icon are text/action: brand green #00B140 on white is 2.85:1 (accepted brand decision); lime in dark 13.7:1. Danger #C50000 6.2:1 (dark #FF5151 5.1:1). Android: Same tokens, same ratios.
- State. Web: No state; danger is shown by red and by the label (Delete). Android: Same.
- Motion. Web: No animation. Android: No animation.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Accepted brand decision: action row labels and the instruction icon use text/action #00B140 on white (2.85:1) in light (ActionCard.tsx, Cards.kt).
- Web action rows are 44 px high, so their 48 px eq-touch areas overlap the next row and the last one is clipped by the card's overflow: hidden; Compose rows are 48 dp (ActionCard.tsx).

Example: WhatsApp reply
```tsx
<ActionCard source="whatsapp" title="WhatsApp · Amit Nanda"
  quote="“Count me in for Sunday 8 PM 👍”" time="03:21"
  actions={[{ label: 'Send', emoji: '📤' }, { label: 'Edit reply', emoji: '✏️' }]} />
```
```kotlin
// The coded WhatsApp logo is the default when no category or icon is set
ActionCard(
    title = "WhatsApp · Amit Nanda",
    quote = "“Count me in for Sunday 8 PM 👍”",
    timestamp = "03:21",
    actions = listOf(
        ActionCardAction("Send", emoji = "📤", onClick = {}),
        ActionCardAction("Edit reply", emoji = "✏️", onClick = {}),
    ),
)
```

Example: Appointment: Confirm + Edit
```tsx
<ActionCard category="others" title="Dr. Mehta's Clinic Appointment"
  details={[
    { text: 'Tomorrow, 9:00 AM' },
    { text: 'Bring previous medical reports', tone: 'secondary' },
  ]}
  time="03:21"
  actions={[{ label: 'Confirm', emoji: '👍' }, { label: 'Edit', emoji: '✏️' }]} />
```
```kotlin
ActionCard(
    category = EqualCategory.Others,
    title = "Dr. Mehta's Clinic Appointment",
    lines = listOf(
        ActionCardLine("Tomorrow, 9:00 AM"),
        ActionCardLine("Bring previous medical reports", ActionCardTone.Tertiary),
    ),
    timestamp = "03:21",
    actions = listOf(
        ActionCardAction("Confirm", emoji = "👍", onClick = {}),
        ActionCardAction("Edit", emoji = "✏️", onClick = {}),
    ),
)
```

Example: Instruction saved
```tsx
<ActionCard icon="instructions" title="Instruction saved"
  details={instructionLines('Delivery agents call', 'Ask them to leave parcels with security')}
  time="03:21" actions={[{ label: 'Edit rule', emoji: '✏️' }]} />
```
```kotlin
ActionCard(
    icon = EqualIcons.Instructions,
    title = "Instruction saved",
    lines = instructionLines("Delivery agents call", "Ask them to leave parcels with security"),
    timestamp = "03:21",
    actions = listOf(ActionCardAction("Edit rule", emoji = "✏️", onClick = {})),
)
```

Example: Instruction (body only)
```tsx
<ActionCardBody icon="instructions" title="Instructions"
  details={instructionLines('Bank calls come', 'Tell callers I’ll call back after 6 PM')}
  time="03:21" />
```
```kotlin
ActionCardBody(
    icon = EqualIcons.Instructions,
    title = "Instructions",
    lines = instructionLines("Bank calls come", "Tell callers I’ll call back after 6 PM"),
    timestamp = "03:21",
)
```

entries.name: assistant-toggle
entries.title: Assistant toggle
entries.summary: The card at the top of Chats and the You tab that turns the AI assistant on or off, with the mascot dimming when it is off.
entries.text:
# Assistant toggle (`assistant-toggle`)
Group: Cards

The card at the top of Chats and the You tab that turns the AI assistant on or off, with the mascot dimming when it is off.

- React: `import { AssistantToggle } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `AssistantToggleCard`
- Tokens: `assistant-toggle/bg`, `bg/surface`, `stroke/subtle`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`, `button/primary`, `button/disabled`, `action/stroke/unread`
- Source: §3 Assistant Availability Toggle

Do: Put it directly under the top bar on Chats (HomeHeader does this) and first under YOUR ASSISTANT on the You tab. Let the default copy explain the state: on manages unknown calls, off lets them ring normally.

Don't: Don't crop or replace the mascot; it dims itself when off. Don't add a Save button; the change applies immediately.

Anatomy:
1. Card: Rounded card whose fill shows on or off. (min height 64 (web) / height 64 (Compose) · padding 12 10 12 12 · radius xl (20) · on: assistant-toggle/bg with an action/stroke/unread glow at each end · off: bg/surface + 1 px stroke/subtle)
2. Mascot: Robot mascot (or the 3D phone experiment) that greys out when off. (Mascot / EqualMascot 36 · off: greyscale, opacity 0.7 · phone art: Asset assistant-phone 36, opacity 0.5 when off)
3. Title: States on or off. (Text subheading · text/primary · one line · "AI Assistant is On / Off")
4. Description: What the state means. (Text caption Regular · text/secondary · one line, ellipsis)
5. Switch: The control. (gap 10 (web) / 12 (Compose) · track 40 × 24 · thumb 18 · on button/primary, thumb text/on-action · off button/disabled, white thumb)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Only the switch is interactive: <button role="switch">; the mascot is role=img. Android: The whole card is toggleable(role = Role.Switch); the inner EqualSwitch has onCheckedChange = null, so it is visual only.
- Name. Web: Switch aria-label "AI Assistant"; the mascot reads "Equal assistant"; the title and description are read as text but are not tied to the switch. Android: The merged card reads the mascot ("Equal assistant"), the title and the description.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to the switch; Space / Enter toggles; the change applies at once. Android: TalkBack: one stop for the card, double-tap to toggle.
- Touch target. Web: The 40 × 24 switch uses eq-touch for a 48 px hit area; the rest of the card is not tappable. Android: The whole 64 dp card is the target.
- Contrast. Web: Title text/primary 12.5:1 and description text/secondary 5.7:1 on both fills. Switch tracks are weak: off #DDDDDD on white 1.36:1 (dark #444444 on #1F1F1F 1.7:1); on is brand green #00B140, 2.85:1 (accepted brand decision). Android: Same tokens, same ratios.
- State. Web: aria-checked on the switch, and the title spells On / Off, so not colour alone. Android: toggleable exposes checked; the title and description change with the state.
- Motion. Web: Track, thumb (500 ms), card and mascot transitions go to 0 ms under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: EqualSwitch animates over 500 ms, 0 ms when Remove animations is on; the card fill changes instantly.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Switch off track button/disabled #DDDDDD on white is 1.36:1 (dark 1.7:1), below 3:1 for a control boundary (Switch.css, EqualSwitch.kt); the title does state On / Off.
- Accepted brand decision: the on track is button/primary #00B140 (2.85:1 on white), just under 3:1 for a control (Switch.css, EqualSwitch.kt).
- AssistantToggleCard fixes the card at height(64.dp), so at large font scales the one-line title and description no longer fit and get clipped; web uses min-height (HomeChrome.kt).

Example: Interactive
```tsx
const [on, setOn] = useState(true);

<AssistantToggle on={on} onChange={setOn} />
```
```kotlin
var on by remember { mutableStateOf(true) }
AssistantToggleCard(checked = on, onCheckedChange = { on = it })
```

Example: On and off
```tsx
<AssistantToggle on />
<AssistantToggle on={false} />
```
```kotlin
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp)) {
    AssistantToggleCard(checked = true, onCheckedChange = {})
    AssistantToggleCard(checked = false, onCheckedChange = {})
}
```

entries.name: feedback-card
entries.title: Feedback card
entries.summary: The post-call card that asks the user to rate the call from one to five stars and share feedback.
entries.text:
# Feedback card (`feedback-card`)
Group: Cards

The post-call card that asks the user to rate the call from one to five stars and share feedback.

- React: `import { FeedbackCard } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `FeedbackCard`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `rating/star-filled`, `rating/star-empty`, `text/placeholder`, `stroke/subtle`, `text/action`
- Source: §13 Feedback Card

Do: Show it once, right after the call summary, indented to line up with the summary bubble. Keep the question short and about the call itself.

Don't: Don't add a text field to the card; Share Feedback opens the next step. Don't use emoji or images for the stars; they are coded.

Anatomy:
1. Card: White card for the rating. (width 246 · bg/surface · radius md (12) · overflow hidden)
2. Question: Asks the user to rate the call. (Text body1 · text/primary · padding 12 10 10)
3. Stars: Five tappable stars. (web: Icon star 32, gap 8, 40 × 48 touch cells · Compose: Icon star 28 centred in 48 dp cells, no gap · filled rating/star-filled · empty outline rating/star-empty)
4. Divider: Separates the rating from the action. (1 px stroke/subtle)
5. Share Feedback: Sends the rating. (40 high (web, TextButton with 48 touch area) / 48 dp (Compose) · Text button text/action · chevron-right 18 (web) / 16 (Compose))

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Stars are <button role="radio"> in a role="radiogroup" aria-label "Rating"; Share is a <button>. Android: Stars use selectable(role = Role.RadioButton) inside a selectableGroup() Row; the Share row is Role.Button.
- Name. Web: Stars aria-label "1 star" … "5 stars"; Share from its text. Android: Star icon contentDescription "1 star" … "5 stars"; Share reads "Share Feedback".
- Keyboard. Web: One Tab stop for the group (roving tabindex); arrow keys and Home / End move focus and the rating. Android: TalkBack: swipe through the stars (announced as a group), double-tap to rate.
- Touch target. Web: Stars use eq-touch at 48 px tall by the 40 px star pitch so neighbours don't overlap; Share's 48 px area sits in a 40 px row at the bottom of a clipped card, so about 44 px is tappable. Android: Each star sits in a 48 dp cell; the Share row is 48 dp high.
- Contrast. Web: Question text/primary 12.6:1. Empty stars (#2B2B2B @ 36%) are 2.1:1 on white (dark 2.9:1); filled stars are brand green #00B140, 2.85:1 (accepted brand decision; lime in dark 13.7:1). Share is text/action at 2.85:1 in light (accepted brand decision). Android: Same tokens, same ratios.
- State. Web: aria-checked on the chosen star; the filled vs outline shape also shows the rating. Android: selected on the chosen star; filled vs outline icon.
- Motion. Web: Star fill transition and press scale go to 0 ms under prefers-reduced-motion; hover previews the rating. Android: No animation.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Empty star outline rating/star-empty is 2.1:1 on white in light (2.9:1 in dark), below 3:1 for a control (FeedbackCard.tsx, Cards.kt).
- Accepted brand decision: filled stars and the Share Feedback label use brand green #00B140 on white (2.85:1) in light (FeedbackCard.tsx, Cards.kt).
- The Share Feedback row is 40 px high at the bottom of a card with overflow: hidden, so the TextButton's 48 px touch area is clipped to about 44 px (FeedbackCard.tsx).

Example: Interactive
```tsx
const [rating, setRating] = useState(0);

<FeedbackCard rating={rating} onRate={setRating} onShare={(r) => submit(r)} />
```
```kotlin
var rating by remember { mutableIntStateOf(0) }
FeedbackCard(
    question = "How would you rate the call?",
    rating = rating,
    onRatingChange = { rating = it },
    // Compose: the share callback takes no argument; read `rating` from state
    onShareFeedbackClick = {},
)
```

Example: Rated
```tsx
<FeedbackCard rating={4} />
```
```kotlin
// Compose: always controlled, so the question and rating callback are required
FeedbackCard(
    question = "How would you rate the call?",
    rating = 4,
    onRatingChange = {},
    onShareFeedbackClick = {},
)
```
