entries.title: Lottie animation
entries.summary: Plays illustrative animations shipped as Lottie JSON: mascot moments, celebrations, typing. The same file plays on web and Android.
entries.text:
# Lottie animation (`lottie`)
Group: Display

Plays illustrative animations shipped as Lottie JSON: mascot moments, celebrations, typing. The same file plays on web and Android.

- React: `import { Lottie } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `EqualLottie`
- Tokens: `text/action`
- Source: Motion · Animations

Do: Use Lottie for illustrative motion; keep micro-interactions (press, toggles, sheets) in code on the motion tokens. Export from After Effects with Bodymovin, shapes only (no images or text layers), 60 fps, under ~100 KB. Tint single-colour animations with `text/action` so they follow the theme.

Don't: Don't rebuild an animation by hand in code when a Lottie file exists. Don't autoplay looping animations behind text people are reading.

Anatomy:
1. Box: Fixed-size container the player draws into. (width / height 120 default · flex-shrink 0 · checkerboard placeholder when the file is missing (web))
2. Animation: Lottie JSON from assets/lottie/, rendered as SVG. (lottie_light svg renderer (web) · LottieAnimation from res/raw/lottie_<name>.json (Compose) · loop / autoplay default true (Compose iterations = IterateForever))
3. Tint: Optional single colour for every fill and stroke. (--eq-lottie-tint (web) · LottieProperty.COLOR / STROKE_COLOR on "**" (Compose) · e.g. text/action)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: With label: role="img"; without: aria-hidden="true". Android: With contentDescription: a semantics contentDescription; without: no semantics.
- Name. Web: The label prop, e.g. "Equal AI is typing". Omit it for decorative motion. Android: The contentDescription parameter.
- Keyboard. Web: Not interactive; no pause control. Android: Not interactive.
- Touch target. Web: Not interactive. Android: Not interactive.
- Contrast. Web: Tint with text/action to follow the theme; a meaningful animation needs 3:1 against its background (brand green on white is 2.85:1, an accepted brand decision; lime on dark passes). Android: Same with EqualTheme.colors.textAction.
- State. Web: No state. Android: No state.
- Motion. Web: Under prefers-reduced-motion it does not autoplay or loop and shows the first frame (read once on mount). Otherwise it loops forever with no pause control. Android: When Remove animations (animator scale 0) is on it shows frame 0 and does not play (read once per context); otherwise it repeats forever.

Known accessibility gaps:
- loop defaults to true with no pause or stop control, so looping animations over 5 s can't be paused (WCAG 2.2.2) unless reduced motion is on (Lottie.tsx, EqualLottie.kt).
- The reduced-motion setting is read once when the player mounts, so turning it on while the animation is showing does not stop it; useReducedMotion in a11y.tsx would follow the change (Lottie.tsx, EqualLottie.kt).

Example: Typing dots
```tsx
// assets/lottie/typing-dots.json
<Lottie name="typing-dots" width={120} height={40} tint="var(--eq-text-action)" label="Equal AI is typing" />
```
```kotlin
// res/raw/lottie_typing_dots.json (copied from assets/lottie/ by `npm run assets`)
EqualLottie(
    rawRes = R.raw.lottie_typing_dots,
    width = 120.dp,
    height = 40.dp,
    tint = EqualTheme.colors.textAction,
    contentDescription = "Equal AI is typing",
)
```

Example: Original colours, play once
```tsx
<Lottie name="typing-dots" width={120} height={40} loop={false} />
```
```kotlin
EqualLottie(rawRes = R.raw.lottie_typing_dots, width = 120.dp, height = 40.dp, iterations = 1)
```

entries.name: address
entries.title: Address
entries.summary: Saved address cards with an Edit / Delete overflow, and the add/edit form (label chips, address lines, city, pincode, guiding direction, Save).
entries.text:
# Address (`address`)
Group: Flows

Saved address cards with an Edit / Delete overflow, and the add/edit form (label chips, address lines, city, pincode, guiding direction, Save).

- React: `import { AddressCard, AddressForm, formatAddress } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `AddressCard`, `AddressForm`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`, `text/danger`, `chip/selected-bg`, `button/primary`
- Source: Flows · Addresses

Do: Use formatAddress so every card reads "line1, line2, City- pincode". Open the form in a titled BottomSheet ("Edit Address" / "Add Address"). Route Delete address through the trash confirm sheet.

Don't: Don't show Edit as a separate button; it lives in the ⋮ menu. Don't accept a pincode that isn't six digits; the form blocks Save.

Anatomy:
1. AddressCard: card: Card for one saved address. (flow card · bg/surface · radius 16 · padding 14/16 · shadow 0 1 2 black/4% · 1dp stroke/subtle in dark)
2. AddressCard: label: Home, Work or a custom name. (subheading · text/primary)
3. AddressCard: address: Full address built by formatAddress. (captionWrap · text/secondary · 4 above)
4. AddressCard: overflow: ⋮ menu with Edit and Delete address. (OverflowMenu 32 · icon 20 · 48 touch area · menu min width 168)
5. AddressForm: label chips: LABEL* overline above Home / Work / Other chips. (overline text/secondary · SegmentedChips 36 high, h16, button token · off bg/surface + 1dp stroke/medium text/secondary · on chip/selected-bg + chip/selected-text)
6. AddressForm: fields: Two address lines, then City and Pincode side by side. (ADDRESS overline · TextField radius 12 · bodyLarge text/primary · min 48 · padding 12/14 · no border in light, stroke/subtle in dark · placeholder text/placeholder · Pincode digits only, 6 max, tabular)
7. AddressForm: error: Message under Pincode when it is not 6 digits. (captionWrap · text/danger · 6 above · field border text/danger)
8. AddressForm: guiding direction: Optional free-text field. (TextField with overline label + '(Optional)' caption Regular text/secondary)
9. AddressForm: Save: Commit. Disabled until line 1, city and a 6-digit pincode are filled. (Button lg block · 45 high · disabled button/disabled + text/on-action-disabled)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: The card is a div. The chips are radios inside a radiogroup. The fields are textarea/input elements. Save is a button. Android: Chips use selectable(Role.RadioButton) inside selectableGroup(). Fields are BasicTextField. Save is Role.Button.
- Name. Web: The overflow is '{label} options'. Fields use aria-label: 'Address line 1', 'Address line 2', 'City', 'Pincode'; Guiding direction uses its visible label. The chip group is labelled by the LABEL* text (aria-labelledby). Android: Overflow contentDescription is '{label} options'. Fields use contentDescription with the same strings. The chip group is 'Address label'.
- Keyboard. Web: The chip group is one Tab stop with arrow keys, Home and End (roving tabIndex). Then the fields and Save. Pincode has inputMode numeric. The overflow menu supports arrows and Escape. Android: TalkBack: swipe through the chips, fields and Save; Pincode opens the number keyboard. Double-tap Save.
- Touch target. Web: Chips (36) and Save (45) use eq-touch for 48. Fields are at least 48. The overflow gets 48 through eq-touch. Android: Chips (36dp) and Save get 48 from minimumInteractiveComponentSize. The overflow trigger uses touchTarget() (48).
- Contrast. Web: Address and overlines text/secondary 5.7:1. Error text/danger 6.2:1. Unselected chip text 5.7:1, selected chip 12.1:1. Placeholders are text/placeholder, 2.85:1. Save is white on green, 2.85:1 in light (accepted brand decision). Android: Same tokens.
- State. Web: Chips use aria-checked. The pincode error sets aria-invalid and is linked with aria-describedby. Save uses native disabled. Android: Chips are selected. The pincode field sets semantics { error() }. Save is enabled = false.
- Motion. Web: Chip colour and field border transitions over duration-base, 0ms under reduced motion. Android: None.

Known accessibility gaps:
- AddressForm in Flows.tsx: Save uses native disabled, so it leaves the Tab order and nothing says which fields are missing.
- AddressForm address, City and Pincode fields (Flows.tsx / Flows.kt) have no visible label; the only visible hint is the placeholder in text/placeholder (2.85:1), which disappears once the user types.
- TextField in light mode (Inputs.css / EqualTextField in Inputs.kt) has a transparent border, so the white field on bg/primary #FAFAFA has about 1.04:1 edge contrast, below 3:1.
- Accepted brand decision: primary buttons put text/on-action white on button/primary #00B140 in light mode, 2.85:1 for 14sp text (Button.css / Buttons.kt). Dark (black on lime) is 17.4:1.

Example: Saved addresses
```tsx
{addresses.map((a) => (
  <AddressCard key={a.id} label={a.label} address={formatAddress(a)}
    onEdit={() => edit(a)} onDelete={() => confirmDelete(a)} />
))}
```
```kotlin
var addresses by remember { mutableStateOf(SampleAddresses) }
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp)) {
    addresses.forEach { a ->
        AddressCard(
            label = a.label,
            address = formatAddress(a),
            onEdit = {},
            onDelete = { addresses = addresses - a },
        )
    }
}
```

Example: Long address
```tsx
<AddressCard label="Work"
  address="Flat 4B, Block C, Skyline Towers, Phase 2, HITECH city, MG Road, Opposite City Center Mall, Banjara Hills, Hyderabad- 500034"
  onEdit={edit} />
```
```kotlin
AddressCard(
    label = "Work",
    address = "Flat 4B, Block C, Skyline Towers, Phase 2, HITECH city, MG Road, Opposite City Center Mall, Banjara Hills, Hyderabad- 500034",
    onEdit = {},
)
```

Example: Edit address form
```tsx
<AddressForm
  initial={{ label: 'Home', line1: 'House no. 4, Tony Street', line2: 'Financial District', city: 'Hyderabad', pincode: '500032' }}
  onSave={(address) => save(address)} />
```
```kotlin
AddressForm(
    // Compose: SavedAddress needs an id (web takes a Partial)
    initial = SavedAddress(
        id = "a1",
        label = "Home",
        line1 = "House no. 4, Tony Street",
        line2 = "Financial District",
        city = "Hyderabad",
        pincode = "500032",
    ),
    onSave = {},
)
```

entries.name: call-handling
entries.title: Call Handling
entries.summary: Pieces of the Call Handling setup and the known-call notification: radio choice cards, contact pickers with an A–Z index, the setup takeover, permission sheets, the done wash, the Android ongoing-call notification and the ongoing-call strip.
entries.text:
# Call Handling (`call-handling`) Group: Flows Pieces of the Call Handling setup and the known-call notification: radio choice cards, contact pickers with an A–Z index, the setup takeover, permission sheets, the done wash, the Android ongoing-call notification and the ongoing-call strip. - React: `import { CallQuestion, ChoiceCard, InfoNote, ContactPick, ContactCheckRow, AlphabetIndex, SetupPrompt, SetupDone, PermissionSheet, CallNotification, OngoingCallBar } from '@equal/ds';` - Compose: `CallQuestion`, `ChoiceCard`, `SuggestedTag`, `InfoNote`, `ContactPick`, `ContactCheckRow`, `AlphabetIndex`, `SetupPrompt`, `SetupDone`, `PermissionSheet`, `CallNotification`, `OngoingCallBar` - Tokens: `choice/default-bg`, `action/fill/unread`, `gradient/choice-stroke`, `info-note/bg`, `initials-disc/bg`, `gradient/setup-done`, `gradient/setup-prompt`, `ongoing-bar/bg`, `ongoing-bar/text` - Source: Known Calls (new users) · Known-call notifications Props of `ChoiceCard`: - `icon`: `IconName`. Leading icon. - `title`: `string`. Option. - `description`: `string`. What it means. - `selected?`: `boolean`. Green outline + tint. - `suggested?`: `boolean`. ⭐ Suggested tag. - `disabled?`: `boolean`. Dimmed (e.g. no permission). - `onSelect?`: `() => void`. Choose. Props of `CallNotification`: - `name`: `string`. Caller. - `state`: `'answering' | 'summary' | 'expanded' | 'connecting'`. Stage of the call. - `category?`: `Category` = 'home-services'. Avatar art. - `elapsed?`: `string` = '00:06'. Timer. - `summary?`: `string`. What the caller wants. - `replies?`: `string[]`. Quick replies (expanded). Props of `PermissionSheet`: - `art`: `AssetName`. 3D art. - `title`: `string`. Ask. - `body`: `ReactNode`. Why. - `cta`: `string`. Action. - `secondary?`: `string`. Underlined text action (e.g. Skip, answer everyone). - `onClose?`: `() => void`. Floating close. Do: Ask for a permission only at the step that needs it, and say why in one line. Keep the notification to who, what they want and one tap to act; Takeover always comes first. Don't: Don't style the notification beyond Android's shell; the system draws it. Don't make the user pick contacts before they've chosen All calls. Anatomy: 1. CallQuestion: Hero art and the setup question. (280 × 208 art or 300 Lottie · title headline Bold (h1) · subtitle title Regular text/secondary · gap 2) 2. ChoiceCard: Radio card for one call-handling option. (radius 20 · padding 18/18/18/20 · gap 16 · choice/default-bg + shadow 0 4 14 black 6% · icon 28 text/primary · title subheading + description body1 text/secondary · 24 radio, 2dp stroke/dark (on: button/primary with 11 dot) · selected: action/fill/unread + 2dp gradient/choice-stroke · disabled 45%) 3. SuggestedTag + InfoNote: Suggested tag on a card, and the note that asks for a permission. (tag ⭐ + caption Regular text/secondary pill, bg/surface, 1dp stroke/subtle, padding 2/8 · note radius 16, info-note/bg, padding 16, gap 4, info 18 + subheading, body1, underlined text/action link with chevron (36 high, 48 touch)) 4. ContactPick: Suggested contact to add or remove. (76 wide · gap 8 · 56 initials disc initials-disc/bg, initials title Medium · 22 +/× badge text/secondary · name body2 Regular) 5. ContactCheckRow + AlphabetIndex: Contact row with a checkbox, and the A–Z jump index. (row padding 10/28/10/16, gap 16 · 52 disc · name title Medium · phone body1 text/secondary tabular · 26 Checkbox (48 touch) · index letters 11/14 Medium text/primary, gap 1) 6. PermissionSheet: Ask-once permission sheet. (bg/primary · radius 32 top · padding 32/20/24 · 110 art · title headline Medium · body title Regular text/secondary · block lg CTA · 44 neutral close top-right (48 touch) · optional underlined secondary link) 7. CallNotification: Android ongoing-call notification while the assistant answers. (radius 24 bg/surface · app line caption text/secondary + 'Ongoing' text/action + timer pill (1dp stroke/subtle) · 40 category avatar · name subheading · summary body1, 1–2 lines · 44 answer ring 1.5dp button/primary or 48 gradient/fab app tile · 34 reply chips gradient/chip-large + action/stroke/unread) 8. SetupPrompt / SetupDone / OngoingCallBar: Setup takeover, done screen and the in-chat call strip. (gradient/setup-prompt takeover, 240 × 169 art, headline Medium + title Regular in white, block lg Start with 1.5dp button/secondary ring · gradient/setup-done wash, 300 × 262 art, 28/34 Bold + block lg Done · bar 44 high, ongoing-bar/bg, graphic-eq 18 + subheading tabular ongoing-bar/text) Accessibility: - Role. Web: ChoiceCard is a button role=radio with aria-checked (the caller adds role=radiogroup with radioGroupKeyDown); ContactCheckRow's control is a role=checkbox; AlphabetIndex is a nav of buttons; PermissionSheet and SetupPrompt are role=dialog; InfoNote is role=note; CallNotification is role=group. Android: ChoiceCard is selectable(Role.RadioButton) (wrap in selectableGroup); the row is toggleable(Role.Checkbox); ContactPick is Role.Button; sheets set paneTitle with a heading(); AlphabetIndex's Column sets paneTitle 'Jump to letter'. - Name. Web: ChoiceCard reads title, Suggested and description; ContactPick 'Add Mom' / 'Remove Vijay Cousin'; checkbox 'Select Arnav Raj'; 'Answer the call'; close 'Close'; notification 'Equal AI is answering Mom'. Android: Same strings via contentDescription; index letters use onClickLabel 'Jump to A'. - Keyboard. Web: With the roving tabindex the radio group is one Tab stop and arrow keys move the selection. PermissionSheet and SetupPrompt use useModal: focus moves in, Tab is trapped and Escape calls onClose. Android: TalkBack reads 'Only unknown numbers, selected, radio button'; double-tap selects. System Back calls the sheet's onClose / onDismiss when set. - Touch target. Web: Reply chips (34) and the answer ring (44) use eq-touch (48); the checkbox has eq-touch and the whole row toggles; Button lg has eq-touch. AlphabetIndex letters fill their 15 px slot and reach 28 px wide. Android: ReplyChip, the answer ring and UnderlinedLink use touchTarget() (48dp); AlphabetIndex letters are 48dp wide but only as tall as their row; ChoiceCard, ContactPick, the row and buttons meet 48dp. - Contrast. Web: Accepted brand decision: the selected radio and choice stroke use button/primary green, 2.8:1 on action/fill/unread; the InfoNote link is 2.7:1 on info-note/bg; primary buttons are white on green 2.85:1. The unselected radio ring (stroke/dark) is 2.2:1. Note text 12.1:1; ongoing bar lime on black 80% is 10.5:1. Dark uses lime with black content. Android: Same tokens and ratios as web. - State. Web: Selected uses aria-checked plus the radio dot and outline; disabled uses the disabled attribute plus 45% opacity; checked uses aria-checked. The notification and ongoing bar announce once through Announce; the ticking timers are not live. Android: selected/enabled on selectable, toggleable state on the row; the summary and 'Ongoing call' are polite live regions, the timers are not. - Motion. Web: SetupPrompt fades in and PermissionSheet slides up; both stop under prefers-reduced-motion. The CallQuestion Lottie shows its first frame. Android: SetupPrompt and PermissionSheet start visible under rememberReduceMotion; EqualLottie doesn't play. Known accessibility gaps: - AlphabetIndex (CallHandling.tsx/.css and CallHandling.kt) letters are only about 15 px/dp tall, far below 48; the 26 letters can't be taller in the column, so the target stays undersized by design. - AlphabetIndex in CallHandling.kt puts paneTitle 'Jump to letter' on a plain Column; paneTitle is for windows and panes, so TalkBack may announce it as a pane change. - The unselected ChoiceCard radio ring (stroke/dark, black 32%) is 2.2:1 on white in CallHandling.css and CallHandling.kt, below 3:1 for a control boundary. - Accepted brand decision: the selected radio and choice stroke (button/primary) are about 2.8:1, the InfoNote link (text/action on info-note/bg) 2.7:1 and primary buttons white on green 2.85:1 in light theme. entries.name: gender-selector
entries.title: Gender selector
entries.summary: The two-card Male / Female picker in Personal Details; the choice sets the profile avatar across the app.
entries.text:
# Gender selector (`gender-selector`)
Group: Flows

The two-card Male / Female picker in Personal Details; the choice sets the profile avatar across the app.

- React: `import { GenderSelector } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `GenderSelector`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `button/primary`, `gradient/gender-selected`, `gradient/gender-selected-stroke`, `gender/stroke`, `text/primary`
- Source: Flows · Profile

Do: Update the profile avatar (hero and bottom nav) as soon as the user picks. Place it under a GENDER overline, below the Name field.

Don't: Don't crop the bust art; if it is missing the card falls back to the ringed avatar. Don't add a third card or a text input here.

Anatomy:
1. Group: Two-column grid of cards. (2 columns · gap 12)
2. Card: One option, Male or Female. (120 high · radius 16 · bg/surface · 2dp gender/stroke border · shadow 0 1 2 black/5% · padding 12 top)
3. Watermark: Faint ♂ or ♀ in the bottom-left corner. (96 · text/primary at 5% · offset -6 / 18 · clipped · decorative)
4. Label: 'Male' or 'Female'. (subheading · text/primary · 12 from the top)
5. Art: Bust for free users; gold-ringed avatar for paid users (or while the bust asset is missing). (bust 60×56 · paid avatar 52 · bottom centre · decorative)
6. Selected state: Gradient outline and lime wash on the chosen card. (gradient/gender-selected over bg/primary · 2dp gradient/gender-selected-stroke (green → lime → green; lime in dark))

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: role="radiogroup" with aria-label 'Gender'. Each card is a button with role="radio". The watermark and art are hidden. Android: The Row has selectableGroup(). Each card is selectable(role = Role.RadioButton).
- Name. Web: Each radio is named only by its text, 'Male' or 'Female' (the avatar has label=""). Android: The card merges its text; the watermark is cleared from semantics and the avatar has contentDescription null.
- Keyboard. Web: One Tab stop (roving tabIndex on the checked card). Arrow keys, Home and End move the selection, as in a native radio group. Android: TalkBack: swipe between the two cards, double-tap to select. TalkBack reads 'selected / not selected'.
- Touch target. Web: Cards are 120 tall and half the width. Android: Cards are 120dp tall and weighted to half the width.
- Contrast. Web: Label 12.6:1. The selected border runs from #00B140 (2.85:1 on white) through lime (1.2:1), so the state indicator is under 3:1 in light (accepted brand decision). In dark it is lime on #1F1F1F, 13.7:1. Android: Same tokens.
- State. Web: aria-checked. Visually, only the border and tint change; there is no check mark. Android: selected = true on the card. Visually, only the border and tint change.
- Motion. Web: Press scale (eq-pressable), 0ms under reduced motion. Android: None.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Accepted brand decision: GenderSelector (Flows.css / Flows.kt) shows the selection only by the green → lime gradient border (2.85:1 to 1.2:1 on white in light) and a faint lime tint, with no check mark.

Example: Free vs paid
```tsx
<GenderSelector value={gender} onChange={setGender} tier="free" />
<GenderSelector value={gender} onChange={setGender} tier="paid" />
```
```kotlin
var gender by remember { mutableStateOf(Gender.Male) }
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(16.dp)) {
    GenderSelector(value = gender, onValueChange = { gender = it }, tier = PlanTier.Free)
    GenderSelector(value = gender, onValueChange = { gender = it }, tier = PlanTier.Paid)
}
```

Example: Interactive
```tsx
const [gender, setGender] = useState<Gender>('male');

<GenderSelector value={gender} onChange={setGender} />
<ProfileAvatar variant={gender} size={56} />
```
```kotlin
var gender by remember { mutableStateOf(Gender.Male) }
GenderSelector(value = gender, onValueChange = { gender = it })
ProfileAvatar(
    variant = if (gender == Gender.Male) ProfileAvatarVariant.Male else ProfileAvatarVariant.Female,
    width = 56.dp,
)
```

Example: In Personal Details
```tsx
<AppBar title="Personal Details" onBack={goBack} />
<TextField label="Name" value={name} onChange={setName}
  helper="Your AI will call you 'Keshav'" />
<SectionHeader inset={0}>Gender</SectionHeader>
<GenderSelector value={gender} onChange={setGender} />
```
```kotlin
var name by remember { mutableStateOf("Keshav") }
var gender by remember { mutableStateOf(Gender.Female) }
EqualAppBar(title = "Personal Details", onBackClick = {})
EqualTextField(
    value = name,
    onValueChange = { name = it },
    label = "Name",
    helper = AnnotatedString("Your AI will call you '$name'"),
)
SectionHeader(title = "Gender", inset = 0.dp)
GenderSelector(value = gender, onValueChange = { gender = it })
```

entries.summary: The pieces of the Instructions flow: recommended cards with a tinted + Apply pill, the New suggestions card, the Active Instructions entry and 3D-art preset cards on the hub, preset and active instruction cards with WHEN / DO rows, and the preview shown in the setup chat.
entries.text:
# Instruction cards (`instruction-cards`)
Group: Flows

The pieces of the Instructions flow: recommended cards with a tinted + Apply pill, the New suggestions card, the Active Instructions entry and 3D-art preset cards on the hub, preset and active instruction cards with WHEN / DO rows, and the preview shown in the setup chat.

- React: `import { RecommendedCard, ApplyButton, SuggestionsComingCard, ActiveInstructionsRow, PresetCard, PresetIcon, PresetInstructionCard, InstructionCard, SourceBadge, WhenDoRow, InstructionPreview } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `RecommendedCard`, `ApplyButton`, `SuggestionsComingCard`, `ActiveInstructionsRow`, `PresetCard`, `PresetIcon`, `PresetInstructionCard`, `InstructionCard`, `SourceBadge`, `WhenDoRow`, `InstructionPreview`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `bg/primary`, `preset/tint-green`, `preset/tint-blue`, `preset/tint-orange`, `preset/tint-lime`, `suggest/glow`, `button/tonal`, `gradient/when-chip`, `gradient/do-chip`, `stroke/subtle`, `stroke/medium`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`, `text/action`, `button/primary`
- Source: Preset Instruction design (For Review)

Do: Write When as the situation and Do as the assistant's behaviour, in plain first person ("say I am not interested"). Use the uppercase WHEN / DO pills on both preset and active instructions. Confirm with 👍 Confirm (unread) next to ✍️ Edit (read) under the preview. Show SuggestionsComingCard once every recommendation is applied.

Don't: Don't delete an instruction straight from the ⋮ menu; confirm first. Don't use Material icons or emoji on preset cards; they lead with their 3D art. Recommended cards lead with emoji. Don't put two filled buttons on a preset instruction; Apply is the only commit.

Anatomy:
1. RecommendedCard: Horizontal card: emoji, the tinted + Apply pill, title and description. (191 wide · min 114 · radius 12 · bg/surface · 1dp stroke/subtle · padding 12 · Emoji 24 · ApplyButton · title 14 SemiBold · description 12/16 text/primary)
2. ApplyButton: Tinted pill that starts the setup chat. (Button sm (24 high) · button/tonal (brand green 8 %, lime 12 % dark) · add 16 + buttonSmall text/action · 48 touch area)
3. SuggestionsComingCard: Shown once every recommendation is applied or none exist. (116 high · radius 16 · bg/primary · 1dp stroke/medium · three suggest/glow circles (blur 50) · orb 18 + 12 Bold text/secondary · body2 13 below, max 184 · illustration-suggestions 140 top-right)
4. ActiveInstructionsRow: Your instructions entry with the robot-with-wand art and the count. (min 76 · radius 16 · 1dp stroke/subtle · mascot-instructions 33 in a 44 preset/tint-lime circle · 14 SemiBold + 12 text/secondary · chevron 22 text/placeholder)
5. PresetCard: Tappable preset: 3D art in a tinted circle, title, description, chevron. (min 85 · radius 16 · 1dp stroke/subtle · PresetIcon 44 (art 33, preset/tint-*) · gap 8 · title 16 SemiBold · description 12/16 text/secondary · chevron 22)
6. PresetInstructionCard: Preset instruction with + Apply, which becomes an 'Applied' pill. (radius 16 · 1dp stroke/subtle · padding 12/16 · gap 16 · title 16/20 SemiBold (h3 web) · ApplyButton · Applied pill 24 action-card/highlight + check 16 + buttonSmall text/action)
7. WhenDoRow: WHEN / DO line, the same on preset and active instructions. (52 × 24 pill gradient/when-chip / gradient/do-chip · 12 SemiBold caps text/secondary · gap 8 · text 14/18 text/primary)
8. SourceBadge: Which preset an active instruction came from. (min 24 · padding 4/8 · bg/surface · 1dp stroke/medium · preset art 16 + 10 SemiBold text/secondary)
9. InstructionCard: Active instruction: bold title + ⋮, source badge, WHEN and DO. No divider. (bg/surface · radius 16 · 1dp stroke/subtle · padding 16 · gap 16 · title 16/20 Bold · badge 6 below · rows gap 12)
10. InstructionPreview: Preview in the setup chat, with an optional ✅ reaction. (ActionCardBody in a bg/surface frame · radius 16 · padding 8 · max 280 · reaction 32 circle bg/surface, shadow/raised, Emoji 18)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: RecommendedCard is a div with an Apply <button>. ActiveInstructionsRow is a <button>. Preset and badge art is decorative (alt ""). PresetCard is a <button>. Instruction titles are h3. The overflow has aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded. Emoji are aria-hidden. Android: Apply, PresetCard and ActiveInstructionsRow are Role.Button. Preset art has no contentDescription. The overflow is Role.Button with Expanded / Collapsed. Titles have no heading(). EmojiGlyph is hidden from TalkBack.
- Name. Web: Apply is 'Apply {title}' on recommended and preset cards. PresetCard is named by its title and description. The overflow is '{title} options'. The ✅ reaction is role="img" 'Confirmed'. Android: Apply's contentDescription is 'Apply {title}'. Overflow: '{title} options'. The ✅ reaction reads 'Confirmed'.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to Apply, the Active Instructions row, the preset cards, Apply and ⋮, then Enter/Space. When Apply becomes 'Applied', focus moves to the pill (useFocusHandoff). Android: TalkBack: swipe through the cards, double-tap to act. Back closes the overflow popup.
- Touch target. Web: The sm Apply pill uses eq-touch for 48. The overflow gets 48 through IconButton. Android: The overflow (32dp) uses touchTarget() for 48dp. Apply (sm) gets 48 from EqualButton.
- Contrast. Web: Titles 12.6:1, descriptions text/secondary 5.7:1, When/Do labels 5.5–5.8:1 in both themes. Below 3:1 in light: the Apply label on button/tonal (≈2.6:1, brand green, accepted) and the Applied text on its highlight (2.59:1), both brand green, and the chevron in text/placeholder (2.85:1). Android: Same tokens. In dark, add and Applied are lime on dark tints, above 10:1.
- State. Web: Applied is shown by the check icon and the 'Applied' text, and a polite Announce says '{title} applied'. Android: Same visuals. The Apply/Applied slot is a polite liveRegion, so the change is announced.
- Motion. Web: Press scale only, 0ms under reduced motion. Android: None.

Known accessibility gaps:
- PresetInstructionCard and InstructionCard in Flows.kt: titles have no heading() semantics (web uses h3).
- The PresetCard and ActiveInstructionsRow chevron (text/placeholder) is 2.85:1 on white in light, below 3:1 (Flows.tsx / Flows.kt).
- Accepted brand decision: the + Apply label (text/action on button/tonal, ≈2.6:1) and the Applied pill (text/action on action-card/highlight, 2.59:1) are below 3:1 in light (Flows.css / Flows.kt).
- The SourceBadge label is 10sp, below the 12sp minimum the rest of the system keeps; it is supplementary (the preset art and the title carry the meaning).

Example: Recommended for you
```tsx
<RecommendedCard emoji="🚫" title="Decline sales & spam"
  description="Politely declines sales and insurance calls." onAdd={add} />
<RecommendedCard emoji="💬" title="Take a message"
  description="Takes their name, number and message." onAdd={add} />

{allApplied && <SuggestionsComingCard />}
```
```kotlin
var added by remember { mutableStateOf(setOf<String>()) }
if (added.size < 2) {
    Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp)) {
        if ("decline" !in added) {
            RecommendedCard(
                emoji = "🚫",
                title = "Decline sales & spam",
                description = "Politely declines sales and insurance calls.",
                onAdd = { added = added + "decline" },
            )
        }
        if ("message" !in added) {
            RecommendedCard(
                emoji = "💬",
                title = "Take a message",
                description = "Takes their name, number and message.",
                onAdd = { added = added + "message" },
            )
        }
    }
} else {
    SuggestionsComingCard()
}
```

Example: Your instructions and browse presets
```tsx
<ActiveInstructionsRow count={5} onClick={openActive} />

<PresetCard art="preset-screen-protect" tint="green" title="Screen & Protect"
  description="Decline spam, hold the line on loan and payments call, close wrong call" onClick={open} />
<PresetCard art="preset-everyday-calls" tint="blue" title="Handle everyday calls"
  description="Take message, guide deliveries, relay to family, start in your language" onClick={open} />
<PresetCard art="preset-business" tint="orange" title="Run my business"
  description="Capture enquiries, orders, bookings, job, and supplier calls" onClick={open} />
```
```kotlin
ActiveInstructionsRow(count = 5, onClick = {})

PresetCard(
    art = PresetArt.ScreenProtect, tint = PresetTint.Green, title = "Screen & Protect",
    description = "Decline spam, hold the line on loan and payments call, close wrong call", onClick = {},
)
PresetCard(
    art = PresetArt.EverydayCalls, tint = PresetTint.Blue, title = "Handle everyday calls",
    description = "Take message, guide deliveries, relay to family, start in your language", onClick = {},
)
PresetCard(
    art = PresetArt.Business, tint = PresetTint.Orange, title = "Run my business",
    description = "Capture enquiries, orders, bookings, job, and supplier calls", onClick = {},
)
```

Example: Preset instructions
```tsx
<PresetInstructionCard instruction={instructionLibrary.declineSales}
  applied={applied} onApply={apply} />
```
```kotlin
var applied by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
PresetInstructionCard(
    instruction = InstructionLibrary.declineSales,
    applied = applied,
    onApply = { applied = true },
)
```

Example: Active instructions
```tsx
<InstructionCard instruction={{
  id: 'decline-sales',
  title: 'Decline sales, promo spam calls',
  source: { art: 'preset-screen-protect', label: 'Screen & Protect' },
  when: 'The caller is selling loan, insurance, credit card, product, or another unsolicited offer',
  do: 'Politely say I am not interested and end the conversation without discussing the offer',
}} onEdit={edit} onDelete={confirmDelete} />
```
```kotlin
InstructionCard(
    instruction = Instruction(
        id = "decline-sales",
        title = "Decline sales, promo spam calls",
        source = InstructionSource(art = PresetArt.ScreenProtect, label = "Screen & Protect"),
        whenText = "The caller is selling loan, insurance, credit card, product, or another unsolicited offer",
        doText = "Politely say I am not interested and end the conversation without discussing the offer",
    ),
    onEdit = {},
    onDelete = {},
)
```

Example: Preview in the setup chat
```tsx
<InstructionPreview title="Decline sales calls"
  when="Caller is selling a loan, insurance or product"
  action="Politely decline and end the conversation"
  time="03:21" confirmed={confirmed} />
```
```kotlin
var confirmed by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
InstructionPreview(
    title = "Decline sales calls",
    whenText = AnnotatedString("Caller is selling a loan, insurance or product"),
    action = AnnotatedString("Politely decline and end the conversation"),
    time = "03:21",
    confirmed = confirmed,
)
```

entries.name: checkbox
entries.title: Checkbox
entries.summary: A coded checkbox with an optional label, used for multi-select such as "Select All" in chat-list selection mode.
entries.text:
# Checkbox (`checkbox`)
Group: Inputs

A coded checkbox with an optional label, used for multi-select such as "Select All" in chat-list selection mode.

- React: `import { Checkbox } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `EqualCheckbox`
- Tokens: `button/primary`, `text/secondary`, `text/primary`
- Source: §5 Chat Header · Selection mode

Do: Use for multi-select lists; the whole label is the tap target. Use bodyLarge labels in headers ("Select All") and body1 in dense lists.

Don't: Don't use a checkbox for an instant on/off setting; that is a Switch. Don't replace the coded box with an image; checkboxes are coded, never images.

Anatomy:
1. Box: The Material checkbox glyph that shows checked or blank. (Icon atom · web 22 default · Compose 18 · checked button/primary · unchecked text/secondary · 48 touch target)
2. Label: Optional text beside the box; part of the same tap target. (web only (Compose rows supply their own text) · gap 12 · bodyLarge 16/400 or body1 14/400 · text/primary · min height 40)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: <button role='checkbox'> with aria-checked; the icon is aria-hidden. Android: toggleable(role = Role.Checkbox) when onCheckedChange is set; with null the row (e.g. SelectionChatHeader Select All) owns it.
- Name. Web: The visible label inside the button; with no label pass ariaLabel (e.g. 'Select Arnav Raj'). Android: contentDescription parameter when nothing beside it names it; otherwise the parent row's merged text.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to focus, Space or Enter toggles. Focus draws shadow/focusRing. Android: TalkBack: swipe to focus, double-tap to toggle; announces 'checked' or 'not checked'.
- Touch target. Web: .eq-touch gives at least a 48px hit area around the 40px-high button (22 × 40 with no label). Android: minimumInteractiveComponentSize() gives 48dp around the 18dp glyph.
- Contrast. Web: Unchecked text/secondary on white is 5.7:1; checked button/primary #00B140 is 2.85:1 in light (accepted brand green, below 3:1); lime in dark passes. Android: Same tokens as web.
- State. Web: aria-checked; the glyph changes from an empty box to a filled box with a tick, so state is not colour alone. There is no disabled prop. Android: toggleableState from toggleable; the glyph changes shape. No enabled parameter.
- Motion. Web: No transition: the glyph swaps instantly, so there is nothing to reduce. Android: No animation; the glyph swaps instantly.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Accepted brand decision: Checkbox.tsx / EqualSwitch.kt checked glyph button/primary #00B140 on white is 2.85:1 in light mode, below 3:1.
- Checkbox.tsx / EqualSwitch.kt (EqualCheckbox): no disabled / enabled support on either platform.

Example: Interactive
```tsx
const [all, setAll] = useState(false);

<Checkbox checked={all} onChange={setAll} label="Select All" />
<Checkbox checked={a} onChange={setA} label="Loan Offers" labelVariant="body1" />
```
```kotlin
var all by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
var loanOffers by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }

// Compose: no label / labelVariant params; put an EqualText beside the box.
Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp), verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) {
    EqualCheckbox(checked = all, onCheckedChange = { all = it })
    EqualText(text = "Select All", style = EqualTheme.type.bodyLarge, color = EqualTheme.colors.textPrimary)
}
Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp), verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) {
    EqualCheckbox(checked = loanOffers, onCheckedChange = { loanOffers = it })
    EqualText(text = "Loan Offers", style = EqualTheme.type.body1, color = EqualTheme.colors.textPrimary)
}
```

Example: Sizes and bare
```tsx
<Checkbox checked size={18} />
<Checkbox checked={false} size={18} />
<Checkbox checked />
<Checkbox checked={false} />
```
```kotlin
Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(20.dp)) {
    EqualCheckbox(checked = true, onCheckedChange = {}, size = 18.dp)
    EqualCheckbox(checked = false, onCheckedChange = {}, size = 18.dp)
    // Compose: default size is 18.dp (web defaults to 22), so pass 22.dp explicitly.
    EqualCheckbox(checked = true, onCheckedChange = {}, size = 22.dp)
    EqualCheckbox(checked = false, onCheckedChange = {}, size = 22.dp)
}
```

Example: In the selection header
```tsx
<SelectionHeader count={selected.length} allSelected={all}
  onSelectAll={(v) => setSelected(v ? ids : [])} />
```
```kotlin
val ids = listOf("arnav", "amit", "priya")
var selected by remember { mutableStateOf(setOf<String>()) }

SelectionChatHeader(
    selectedCount = selected.size,
    allSelected = selected.size == ids.size,
    onSelectAllChange = { all -> selected = if (all) ids.toSet() else emptySet() },
    onBackClick = {},
    onMarkReadClick = {},
    onDeleteClick = {},
)
```

entries.text:
# Composer (`composer`)
Group: Inputs

The message input bar with a send button that stays disabled until there is text, used at the bottom of a chat and in the AI panel.

- React: `import { Composer } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `VoiceInputBar`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `stroke/subtle`, `action/stroke/unread`, `shadow/focusRing`, `gradient/send-disabled`, `gradient/fab`, `shadow/fab`, `text/secondary`, `text/primary`
- Source: §15 Voice Input Bar (Composer)

Do: Pin the composer to the bottom of the chat or AI panel. Leave send disabled on empty input; the component does this for you.

Don't: Don't add attachment or emoji buttons inside the bar; the spec is input + send only. Don't change the send glyph; it is the coded send icon rotated −35°.

Anatomy:
1. Input: Pill text field where the user types a message. (45 high · radius full · padding h20 · bg/surface · 1px stroke/subtle · focus action/stroke/unread + shadow/focusRing · body1 14/400 text/primary)
2. Placeholder: Hint shown while empty. (web 'Type a message...' · Compose 'Type a message' · body1 · text/secondary)
3. Send button: Circle that sends the message; enabled only when there is text. (45 circle · gap 10 · disabled gradient/send-disabled · active gradient/fab + shadow/fab · 48 touch target)
4. Send icon: Paper-plane glyph rotated −35°. (Icon atom · send 20 · active text/on-action · disabled text/on-dark)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: <form> with a native <input> and a <button type='submit'>. Android: BasicTextField plus a Box with clickable(role = Role.Button).
- Name. Web: Input aria-label 'Message'; send button aria-label 'Send'. Android: Input contentDescription 'Message'; send uses sendContentDescription ('Send') as both onClickLabel and icon description.
- Keyboard. Web: Enter submits the form; Tab moves to Send, which is skipped while disabled. Focus draws shadow/focusRing. Android: IME action Send calls onSend when there is text; TalkBack double-tap on the send button. The send button has no visible hardware-keyboard focus.
- Touch target. Web: Send is 45px with .eq-touch for a 48px hit area; the input is 45px high, full width. Android: touchTarget() gives the 45dp send circle a 48dp area without changing the layout.
- Contrast. Web: Text 12.6:1, placeholder text/secondary 5.7:1. Active send icon is white on gradient/fab (#BAFF29 → #00B140), 1.2–2.85:1 in light (accepted brand gradient); dark is black on lime (about 17:1). Android: Same tokens as web.
- State. Web: Send uses the native disabled attribute until there is text; the fill also changes. Android: clickable(enabled = canSend) exposes disabled; enabled = false on the bar disables both.
- Motion. Web: Border, ring and send shadow fade over 200ms; press scale on send; zeroed under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: Press scale on send via eqPressFeedback, following the system animator scale; border changes instantly.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Accepted brand decision: Composer.css / Composer.kt active send icon is white on gradient/fab (#BAFF29 → #00B140), 1.2–2.85:1 in light mode, below 3:1.
- Composer.kt: SendButton uses indication = null with no focus ring, so hardware-keyboard focus on it is invisible.

Example: Interactive
```tsx
<Composer onSend={(text) => setSent((s) => [...s, text])} />
```
```kotlin
val sent = remember { mutableStateListOf<String>() }
var text by remember { mutableStateOf("") }

// Compose: always controlled; clear the value yourself after send.
VoiceInputBar(
    value = text,
    onValueChange = { text = it },
    onSend = {
        sent += text.trim()
        text = ""
    },
)
```

Example: States
```tsx
<Composer />
<Composer forceFocus />
<Composer value="Sure, I'll be there!" onChange={setText} />
```
```kotlin
var text by remember { mutableStateOf("Sure, I'll be there!") }

Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(16.dp)) {
    VoiceInputBar(value = "", onValueChange = {}, onSend = {})
    // Compose: no forceFocus; the focused look appears when the field has focus.
    VoiceInputBar(value = text, onValueChange = { text = it }, onSend = {})
}
```

entries.name: search
entries.title: Search
entries.summary: The search screen’s pieces: the outlined search bar with back inside, section labels with Clear all, recent searches as avatar tiles, message hits with the match in bold, loading dots and the three illustration states.
entries.text:
# Search (`search`)
Group: Inputs

The search screen’s pieces: the outlined search bar with back inside, section labels with Clear all, recent searches as avatar tiles, message hits with the match in bold, loading dots and the three illustration states.

- React: `import { SearchBar, SearchSection, RecentSearches, MessageResult, LoadingDots, SearchState } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `SearchBar`, `SearchSection`, `RecentSearches`, `MessageResult`, `LoadingDots`, `SearchState`
- Tokens: `button/primary`, `bg/surface`, `text/secondary`, `text/primary`
- Source: Search

Props of `SearchBar`:
- `value`: `string`. Query.
- `onChange?`: `(v: string) => void`. Typing.
- `onBack?`: `() => void`. Back arrow inside the bar.
- `placeholder?`: `string` = 'Search for names'. Hint.

Props of `MessageResult`:
- `name`: `string`. Who.
- `time`: `string`. When.
- `text`: `string`. The message line.
- `query`: `string`. Bolded wherever it appears.

Props of `SearchState`:
- `art`: `AssetName`. Illustration.
- `title`: `string`. Headline.
- `body`: `string`. One line of help.
- `size?`: `number` = 160. Art size.

Do: Show chats first and messages after; chats come back fastest. Bold the match in message hits so people see why each one showed up.

Don't: Don't show a spinner for the whole screen; load each section in place with the dots. Don't reuse the no-results art for errors; offline has its own.

Anatomy:
1. SearchBar: Pill search field with back inside and clear once there is a query. (52 high · margin 8/16 · radius full · bg/surface · 1.5dp button/primary outline · back 40 (48 touch) arrow 22 text/primary · bodyLarge input, placeholder text/secondary, caret text/action · clear × 18 text/secondary (48 touch))
2. SearchSection: Section label with optional Clear all. (overline uppercase text/secondary · padding 14/16/8 · h2 on web, heading() in Compose · Clear all caption pill bg/surface, padding 4/12 (48 touch))
3. RecentSearches: Recent searches as avatar tiles. (72 wide tiles · gap 14 · 52 avatar (decorative) · caption Regular name, truncated)
4. MessageResult: A message hit with the match in bold. (padding 10/16 · name subheading + time micro text/secondary · line body1, match Bold text/primary · 1dp stroke/subtle between hits)
5. LoadingDots: Three dots that pulse while a section loads. (9 dots · gap 8 · button/primary · pulse 1s, staggered 0.15s · padding 24)
6. SearchState: Illustration state: start, no internet, no results. (art 160 (100–120 in use) · title title Medium (h2 on web, heading() in Compose) · body body1 text/secondary, max 280)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Input is a plain text input (not type=search); back, clear, Clear all, tiles and hits are buttons; LoadingDots is role=status; SearchSection labels and SearchState titles are h2. Android: BasicTextField with contentDescription; back and clear are Role.Button; LoadingDots is a polite live region; section labels and SearchState titles are heading().
- Name. Web: Input named by its placeholder ('Search for names'); 'Back'; 'Clear search'; 'Clear all'; tiles by their label (the avatar is decorative); hits by name, time and line. Android: Same strings; recent tiles have onClickLabel 'Search Amit Nanda'.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab: back, input, clear; Enter/Space on buttons. The input has autoFocus when asked. Android: TalkBack: swipe to the field and double-tap to edit; double-tap tiles and hits.
- Touch target. Web: Back, clear and Clear all use eq-touch (48); tiles 72 wide; hits full width. Android: Back, clear and Clear all use minimumInteractiveComponentSize; tiles and hits are large rows.
- Contrast. Web: Placeholder and section labels text/secondary 5.7:1 on white; highlight Bold text/primary 12.6:1. Accepted brand decision: the green bar outline and loading dots (button/primary) are 2.85:1 in light; lime in dark. Android: Same tokens and ratios as web.
- State. Web: The match is shown by weight (Bold), not colour. Loading is announced via role=status 'Loading'. Result counts are not announced. Android: Loading is announced by the live region; matches are bolded.
- Motion. Web: LoadingDots pulse; stopped under prefers-reduced-motion (dots stay solid). Android: LoadingDots stop under rememberReduceMotion.

Known accessibility gaps:
- SearchBar input in Search.tsx is a plain text input, so it isn't exposed as a search field; use type="search" (or role="searchbox").
- Accepted brand decision: SearchBar outline and LoadingDots use button/primary at 2.85:1 in light theme, under 3:1 for UI parts (Search.css and Search.kt).

Example: Search bar
```tsx
<SearchBar value={q} onChange={setQ} onBack={goBack} autoFocus />
```
```kotlin
var q by remember { mutableStateOf("") }
SearchBar(value = q, onValueChange = { q = it }, onBack = {}, autoFocus = true)
```

Example: Recent searches
```tsx
<SearchSection title="Recent searches" onClear={clearRecent} />
<RecentSearches items={recent} onPick={setQ} />
```
```kotlin
var q by remember { mutableStateOf("") }
var recent by remember {
    mutableStateOf(
        listOf(
            RecentSearch("Amit Nanda", EqualCategory.Career),
            RecentSearch("Shankar", EqualCategory.Ride),
            RecentSearch("DSR Builder", EqualCategory.Financial),
        ),
    )
}
Column {
    SearchBar(value = q, onValueChange = { q = it })
    SearchSection(title = "Recent searches", onClear = { recent = emptyList() })
    RecentSearches(items = recent, onPick = { q = it })
}
```

Example: Message results
```tsx
<MessageResult name="Santosh Anna" time="3:02 PM" text={line} query={q} onClick={openMessage} />
```
```kotlin
val q = "Sa"
Column {
    SearchSection(title = "Messages")
    MessageResult(name = "Santosh Anna", time = "3:02 PM", text = "Caller said that they’ll call you in the evening", query = q, onClick = {})
    EqualDivider()
    MessageResult(name = "Amit Nanda", time = "3:02 PM", text = "Same address, near Gachibowli", query = q, onClick = {})
}
```

Example: States
```tsx
<SearchState art="illustration-search" title="Search across your calls" body="…" />
<SearchState art="illustration-no-internet" title="No internet connection" body="…" />
<SearchState art="illustration-no-results" title="No results found" body="…" />
<LoadingDots />
```
```kotlin
Column {
    // Compose: SearchState takes an EqualAssets illustration and a size in dp
    SearchStateView(art = EqualAssets.IllustrationSearch, size = 170.dp, title = "Search across your calls", body = "Look for names, phone numbers, categories, keywords")
    SearchStateView(art = EqualAssets.IllustrationNoInternet, size = 130.dp, title = "No internet connection", body = "We could not connect to a stable internet. Check your connection and try again.")
    SearchStateView(art = EqualAssets.IllustrationNoResults, size = 150.dp, title = "No results found", body = "Couldn’t find anything matching. Try a different name, number, category or keyword")
    LoadingDots()
}
```

entries.name: search-field
entries.title: Search field
entries.summary: A pill search input with a leading search icon and a clear button, used to filter chats.
entries.text:
# Search field (`search-field`)
Group: Inputs

A pill search input with a leading search icon and a clear button, used to filter chats.

- React: `import { SearchField } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `SearchField`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `text/secondary`, `text/primary`, `text/placeholder`
- Source: Surfaces from the Typography screen inventory · Search Field

Do: Say what is being searched in the placeholder ("Search chats"). Show an EmptyState with the query in it when nothing matches.

Don't: Don't add a separate search button; results filter as you type. Don't use it as a general form field; use TextField.

Anatomy:
1. Container: Full-width pill that holds the search input. (48 high · radius full · bg/surface · web 1px stroke/subtle border, focus action/stroke/unread + shadow/focusRing · padding web 16 start / 14 end, Compose h16 · Compose no border)
2. Search icon: Leading magnifier that marks the field as search. (Icon atom · search 20 · text/secondary · gap web 10, Compose 8 · decorative)
3. Input / placeholder: The query text, or 'Search for names' while empty. (bodyLarge 16/400 · text/primary · placeholder web text/secondary, Compose text/placeholder)
4. Clear button: Web only: appears once there is text and empties the field. (close 18 · text/secondary · .eq-touch 48 hit area · aria-label 'Clear')

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Native <input> inside a <label>; with onActivate it becomes a readOnly input that hands off to the search screen. Android: BasicTextField when editable; with onActivate a Row with clickable(role = Role.Button).
- Name. Web: aria-label is the placeholder ('Search for names'); the clear button is 'Clear'. Android: contentDescription (default the placeholder) on the editable field; the onActivate row reads the placeholder text with onClickLabel = placeholder.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to the input, type; Tab again reaches Clear. With onActivate, focusing the input blurs it at once and calls onActivate. Android: TalkBack: double-tap to edit; the onActivate variant is a button, double-tap opens search.
- Touch target. Web: Container 48px high; Clear gets 48px via .eq-touch. Android: 48dp high, full width.
- Contrast. Web: Text 12.6:1; placeholder and icon text/secondary on white 5.7:1 (dark 6.7:1). The 1px stroke/subtle border is 1.1:1. Android: Icon text/secondary 5.7:1, but the placeholder uses text/placeholder (2.85:1 on white), lower than web.
- State. Web: Clear appears only when there is a value; focus shows the green border and ring. Android: No clear control and no focus styling.
- Motion. Web: Border and ring fade over 200ms; zeroed under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: None.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Inputs.tsx: with onActivate the field is a readOnly input that blurs itself on focus, so keyboard and screen-reader users lose focus; it should be a <button> styled as the field.
- Inputs.kt: the editable SearchField has no clear button and no focus border or ring (web has both).
- Inputs.kt: SearchField placeholder uses text/placeholder (2.85:1 on white) where web uses text/secondary (5.7:1).

Example: Empty
```tsx
const [q, setQ] = useState('');

<SearchField value={q} onChange={setQ} />
```
```kotlin
var q by remember { mutableStateOf("") }

// Compose: the default placeholder is "Search", so pass "Search chats".
SearchField(value = q, onValueChange = { q = it }, placeholder = "Search chats")
```

Example: With a query
```tsx
<SearchField value="Amit" onChange={setQ} />
```
```kotlin
var q by remember { mutableStateOf("Amit") }

// Compose: no built-in clear (X) button; clear by setting the value to "".
SearchField(value = q, onValueChange = { q = it }, placeholder = "Search chats")
```

Example: Filtering the chat list
```tsx
<SearchField value={q} onChange={setQ} />
{results.length === 0
  ? <EmptyState title="No chats found" body={`Nothing matches "\${q}". Try a name or number.`} />
  : results.map((c) => <ChatListItem key={c.id} {...c} />)}
```
```kotlin
val chats = listOf("Arnav Raj", "Amit Kumar", "Priya Nair")
var q by remember { mutableStateOf("") }
val results = chats.filter { it.contains(q, ignoreCase = true) }

SearchField(value = q, onValueChange = { q = it }, placeholder = "Search chats")
if (results.isEmpty()) {
    EmptyState(title = "No chats found", body = "Nothing matches \"$q\". Try a name or number.")
} else {
    results.forEach { name ->
        ChatListItem(name = name, preview = "You have a visitor", date = "Yesterday")
    }
}
```

entries.name: segmented-chips
entries.title: Segmented chips
entries.summary: A single-select row of pill chips for a short, fixed set of options, like the Home / Work / Other address label.
entries.text:
# Segmented chips (`segmented-chips`)
Group: Inputs

A single-select row of pill chips for a short, fixed set of options, like the Home / Work / Other address label.

- React: `import { SegmentedChips } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `SegmentedChips`
- Tokens: `chip/selected-bg`, `chip/selected-text`, `stroke/medium`, `text/secondary`
- Source: Surfaces from the Typography screen inventory · Segmented Label Chips

Do: Use for two to four short options where exactly one is always selected. Declare options `as const` so value and onChange are typed to the union.

Don't: Don't use it for multi-select; use checkboxes. Don't use it for long labels that would wrap; the chips wrap as a row, not the text.

Anatomy:
1. Group: Row of mutually exclusive chips (Home / Work / Other). (gap 8 · wraps on web · named by `label` / `labelledBy` (web) or contentDescription (Compose))
2. Chip: One option pill. (36 high · padding h16 · radius full · 1px stroke/medium · bg/surface · 48 touch target)
3. Label: The option name. (Text atom · button 14/500 · text/secondary)
4. Selected chip: The chosen option, filled dark. (fill + border chip/selected-bg (#313131 light, #F7F7F7 dark) · label chip/selected-text)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: role='radiogroup' on the row and <button role='radio'> per chip. Android: selectableGroup() on the Row and selectable(role = Role.RadioButton) per chip.
- Name. Web: Each chip is named by its label; the group by `label` (aria-label) or `labelledBy`. Android: Each chip by its text; the group by the contentDescription parameter.
- Keyboard. Web: One Tab stop (roving tabindex on the checked chip); arrow keys and Home / End move focus and selection, wrapping. Focus draws shadow/focusRing. Android: TalkBack: swipe between options, double-tap to select; announces 'selected' and position in the group.
- Touch target. Web: .eq-touch gives each 36px chip a 48px hit area. Android: minimumInteractiveComponentSize() gives 48dp around the 36dp chip.
- Contrast. Web: Unselected text/secondary on white 5.7:1; selected #F7F7F7 on #313131 12.1:1 (inverted in dark). The stroke/medium border is 1.2:1; the label identifies each chip. Android: Same tokens as web.
- State. Web: aria-checked on the selected radio; selection is a full fill swap, not just a hue change. Android: selected = true is exposed by selectable.
- Motion. Web: Fill, colour and border fade over 200ms, plus press scale; zeroed under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: No animation.

Example: Address label
```tsx
const LABELS = ['Home', 'Work', 'Other'] as const;
const [label, setLabel] = useState<(typeof LABELS)[number]>('Home');

<SegmentedChips options={LABELS} value={label} onChange={setLabel} />
```
```kotlin
val labels = listOf("Home", "Work", "Other")
var selected by remember { mutableStateOf(0) }

SegmentedChips(options = labels, selectedIndex = selected, onSelectedIndexChange = { selected = it })
```

Example: Any string union
```tsx
const SPEEDS = ['Slow', 'Normal', 'Fast'] as const;

<SegmentedChips options={SPEEDS} value={v} onChange={setV} />
```
```kotlin
val speeds = listOf("Slow", "Normal", "Fast")
var selected by remember { mutableStateOf(1) }

// Compose: options are a List<String> addressed by index, not a typed union.
SegmentedChips(options = speeds, selectedIndex = selected, onSelectedIndexChange = { selected = it })
```

entries.name: switch
entries.title: Switch
entries.summary: A controlled on/off toggle (40 × 24 track) for settings that take effect immediately, such as the assistant or promotional-call muting.
entries.text:
# Switch (`switch`)
Group: Inputs

A controlled on/off toggle (40 × 24 track) for settings that take effect immediately, such as the assistant or promotional-call muting.

- React: `import { Switch } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `EqualSwitch`
- Tokens: `button/primary`, `button/disabled`, `brand/white`, `shadow/raised`
- Source: §3 Assistant Availability Toggle · Switch

Do: Use a Switch when the change applies instantly (Mute Promotional Calls, Get updates on WhatsApp). Put the visible label in the row beside it and pass the same text as `label`. Confirm with a sheet when turning something off has consequences, as WhatsApp Updates does ("Turn off WhatsApp updates?").

Don't: Don't use a Switch for a choice that needs a Save button; use Checkbox or SegmentedChips. Don't recolour the track; on is button/primary and off is button/disabled in both themes.

Anatomy:
1. Track: The pill that shows on or off and takes the tap. (40 × 24 · radius full · on button/primary · off button/disabled · 48 touch target)
2. Thumb: The circle that slides to the on side. (18 circle · inset 3 · travel 16 · shadow/raised · on text/on-action (white in light, black on lime in dark) · off brand white)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: <button role='switch'> with aria-checked. Android: toggleable(role = Role.Switch) when onCheckedChange is set; with null the parent row (AssistantToggleCard, ToggleRow) owns the semantics.
- Name. Web: Required `label` prop set as aria-label (match the visible row label, e.g. 'AI Assistant'); `describedBy` links the description. Android: contentDescription parameter for a standalone switch; inside a row pass onCheckedChange = null and the row's merged text names it.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to focus, Space or Enter toggles; disabled removes it from the tab order. Focus draws shadow/focusRing. Android: TalkBack: swipe to focus, double-tap to toggle; it announces 'on' or 'off'.
- Touch target. Web: .eq-touch gives a 48px hit area around the 40 × 24 track. Android: minimumInteractiveComponentSize() on the toggleable gives 48dp; a parent row usually supplies a larger target.
- Contrast. Web: On track #00B140 on white is 2.85:1 (accepted brand green); off track #DDDDDD is 1.36:1, both below 3:1. Dark: lime on #1F1F1F 13.7:1, off #444444 1.7:1. Thumb position also shows state. Android: Same tokens as web.
- State. Web: aria-checked true/false; the thumb moves right as well as changing colour, so state is not colour alone. Disabled uses the disabled attribute and 50% opacity. Android: toggleableState is announced; enabled = false sets disabled semantics but draws no visual change.
- Motion. Web: Track and thumb animate over motion.switchToggle (500ms ease-in-out); base.css zeroes it under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: Thumb offset and track colour tween over 500ms, set to 0ms when rememberReduceMotion() is true.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Accepted brand decision: Switch.css / EqualSwitch.kt on track button/primary #00B140 on white is 2.85:1, below the 3:1 non-text minimum.
- Switch.css / EqualSwitch.kt: off track button/disabled #DDDDDD on white is 1.36:1 (dark #444444 on #1F1F1F is 1.7:1), below 3:1.
- EqualSwitch.kt: enabled = false changes nothing visually (web dims to 50%).

Example: Interactive
```tsx
const [on, setOn] = useState(true);

<Switch checked={on} onChange={setOn} label="AI Assistant" />
```
```kotlin
var on by remember { mutableStateOf(true) }

// Compose: no label param; set the accessible label with semantics.
EqualSwitch(
    checked = on,
    onCheckedChange = { on = it },
    modifier = Modifier.semantics { contentDescription = "AI Assistant" },
)
```

Example: States
```tsx
<Switch checked label="On" />
<Switch checked={false} label="Off" />
<Switch checked disabled label="On, disabled" />
<Switch checked={false} disabled label="Off, disabled" />
```
```kotlin
Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(20.dp)) {
    EqualSwitch(checked = true, onCheckedChange = {})
    EqualSwitch(checked = false, onCheckedChange = {})
    EqualSwitch(checked = true, onCheckedChange = {}, enabled = false)
    EqualSwitch(checked = false, onCheckedChange = {}, enabled = false)
}
```

Example: In context
```tsx
<RowGroup>
  <ToggleRow label="Mute Promotional Calls" wrap
    description="Equal AI Assistant can identify Promotional Calls and automatically mute them"
    checked={mute} onChange={setMute} />
</RowGroup>
```
```kotlin
var mute by remember { mutableStateOf(true) }

RowGroup {
    ToggleRow(
        label = "Mute Promotional Calls",
        description = "Equal AI Assistant can identify Promotional Calls and automatically mute them",
        descriptionWraps = true,
        checked = mute,
        onCheckedChange = { mute = it },
    )
}
```

entries.name: text-field
entries.title: Text field
entries.summary: A borderless white form field with an uppercase overline label, bodyLarge value, helper and error text, used in the Personal Details and Address forms.
entries.text:
# Text field (`text-field`)
Group: Inputs

A borderless white form field with an uppercase overline label, bodyLarge value, helper and error text, used in the Personal Details and Address forms.

- React: `import { TextField } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `EqualTextField`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `stroke/medium`, `action/stroke/unread`, `shadow/focusRing`, `text/primary`, `text/placeholder`, `text/secondary`, `text/danger`
- Source: Surfaces from the Typography screen inventory · Text Field

Do: Write the overline label in the string's natural case; the component uppercases it (rule 5). Use `pill` for single short values (Name) and `rounded` for address lines. Add `className="eq-tnum"` on numeric fields; postal codes use tabular figures (rule 6).

Don't: Don't add a border in light mode; fields are borderless white on bg/primary. Don't put instructions in the placeholder that the user needs after typing; use `helper`. Don't show both helper and error; the error replaces the helper.

Anatomy:
1. Label: Uppercase overline that names the field, with * when required. (Text atom · overline 11/500 · text/secondary · margin-bottom 8)
2. Optional marker: '(Optional)' after the label for fields the user may skip. (caption Regular 12/400 · text/secondary · gap 6)
3. Input container: The surface the user types into. (min height 48 · radius/md 12 · padding 12 / 14 · bg/surface · 1px border transparent in light, stroke/subtle in dark · focus action/stroke/unread + shadow/focusRing · error text/danger border)
4. Value / placeholder: The entered text, or a hint while empty. (bodyLarge 16/400 · text/primary · placeholder text/placeholder · multiline 2 rows · optional centre align and tabular figures (Compose))
5. Helper or error: One line below the field: guidance, or the error that replaces it. (captionWrap 12/400 · margin-top 6 · helper text/secondary · error text/danger)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Native <input> or <textarea> (textbox). Android: BasicTextField (editable text node).
- Name. Web: A <label htmlFor> wraps the overline, but aria-label={label} overrides it, so the name is the raw label without '(Optional)'. Fields without a label take aria-label from props. Android: contentDescription ?: label is set in semantics on the field; pass contentDescription when a group shares one label.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to focus, type; textarea accepts Enter for new lines. Android: TalkBack: double-tap to edit; keyboardOptions sets the IME type and action.
- Touch target. Web: Input min height 48px, full width. Android: heightIn(min = 48.dp), full width.
- Contrast. Web: Value text/primary 12.6:1; label text/secondary on bg/primary 5.7:1; error text/danger 6.0:1; placeholder text/placeholder 2.85:1. In light the field edge is white on #FAFAFA (1.04:1) and the focus border action/stroke/unread is 1.5:1. Android: Same tokens; dark mode adds a stroke/subtle border (1.3:1 on #1F1F1F).
- State. Web: Error sets aria-invalid and a red border, and aria-describedby links the error or helper text; required sets aria-required and shows '*'. Android: enabled maps to disabled semantics; error is set with semantics { error(...) }, so TalkBack announces it on focus. Required is only the '*' in the label text.
- Motion. Web: Border and focus ring fade over 200ms; zeroed under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: No animation; border colour switches instantly.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Inputs.tsx: aria-label={label} overrides the <label>, so the accessible name drops '(Optional)'.
- Inputs.kt: required is not exposed to TalkBack; the field's contentDescription is the bare label and only the separate label text carries '*'.
- Inputs.css / Inputs.kt: in light mode the field has a transparent border, so its edge is white on bg/primary #FAFAFA (1.04:1), below 3:1.
- Inputs.css / Inputs.kt: placeholder text/placeholder (black at 40%) on white is 2.85:1, below 4.5:1.

Example: Name
```tsx
const [name, setName] = useState('Keshav');

<TextField label="Name" value={name} onChange={setName}
  placeholder="Your name" helper="Your AI will call you 'Keshav'" />
```
```kotlin
var name by remember { mutableStateOf("Keshav") }

EqualTextField(
    value = name,
    onValueChange = { name = it },
    label = "Name",
    placeholder = "Your name",
    helper = AnnotatedString("Your AI will call you 'Keshav'"),
)
```

Example: Optional label
```tsx
<TextField label="Guiding direction" optional value={v} onChange={setV}
  placeholder="e.g. Near City Center Mall" />
```
```kotlin
var direction by remember { mutableStateOf("") }

EqualTextField(
    value = direction,
    onValueChange = { direction = it },
    label = "Guiding direction",
    optional = true,
    placeholder = "e.g. Near City Center Mall",
)
```

Example: Multiline and grouped
```tsx
<TextField aria-label="Address line 1" placeholder="Flat, house no., building"
  value={l1} onChange={setL1} multiline />
<TextField aria-label="Address line 2" placeholder="Street, area, landmark"
  value={l2} onChange={setL2} multiline />
```
```kotlin
var line1 by remember { mutableStateOf("") }
var line2 by remember { mutableStateOf("") }

// Fields that share one ADDRESS label omit `label` and pass contentDescription instead.
EqualTextField(
    value = line1,
    onValueChange = { line1 = it },
    contentDescription = "Address line 1",
    placeholder = "Flat, house no., building",
    multiline = true,
)
EqualTextField(
    value = line2,
    onValueChange = { line2 = it },
    contentDescription = "Address line 2",
    placeholder = "Street, area, landmark",
    multiline = true,
)
```

Example: Error
```tsx
<TextField aria-label="Pincode" placeholder="Pincode" value={pin}
  onChange={(v) => setPin(v.replace(/\D/g, '').slice(0, 6))}
  inputMode="numeric" className="eq-tnum" align="center"
  error={/^\d{6}$/.test(pin) ? undefined : 'Enter a 6-digit pincode'} />
```

```kotlin
var pin by remember { mutableStateOf("") }

EqualTextField(
    value = pin,
    onValueChange = { pin = it.filter(Char::isDigit).take(6) },
    contentDescription = "Pincode",
    placeholder = "Pincode",
    keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Number),
    tabular = true,

```

entries.text:
# Call history (`call-history`)
Group: Lists & rows

The Contact Info call-history card (radius 16; outlined in dark) and its rows: direction icon, call type, meta line and time.

- React: `import { CallHistoryList, CallHistoryRow } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `CallHistoryList`, `CallHistoryRow`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `stroke/subtle`, `stroke/medium`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`, `text/danger`
- Source: Contact Info · Call history

Do: Separate date and duration in `meta` with " • " ("Today • 30 Sec."). Group rows in a CallHistoryList under a `SectionHeader size="label"` CALL HISTORY header (inset 22).

Don't: Don't colour the "Missed Call" label red; only the icon uses text/danger. Don't pass your own label; the direction sets it.

Anatomy:
1. List card: Rounded card that holds the call rows. (inset 22 · radius 16 · bg/surface · 1dp dividers stroke/subtle (stroke/medium in dark) · dark adds a 1dp stroke/subtle outline)
2. Direction icon: Incoming, outgoing or missed arrow. Only the missed icon is red. (Icon 24 · text/primary, text/danger when missed · 10 to the text)
3. Call type: Label set by the direction: Incoming Call, Outgoing Call or Missed Call. (bodyLarge, line height 20 · text/primary)
4. Meta line: Date and duration, e.g. 'Today • 30 Sec.'. (micro Regular 11/14 · text/secondary)
5. Time: Time of the call. (body1 · text/secondary · tabular)
6. Trailing: Optional content after the time, e.g. a play or call-back button. (web: any node (e.g. IconButton 32/20) · Compose: onCallClick adds a 48dp PlainIconButton call in text/action)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: The card is role="list" with aria-label 'Call history' and each row is role="listitem". The direction icon is aria-hidden. Android: CallHistoryList sets collectionInfo (rowCount = itemCount). Each row merges its texts into one item; the icon has contentDescription null.
- Name. Web: Each row reads as its text: call type, meta, time. Direction comes from the 'Missed Call' text, not the icon. Android: TalkBack reads one stop per call (label, meta, time). The call button is a separate stop, 'Call back'.
- Keyboard. Web: Rows are not focusable. A trailing IconButton is reached with Tab. Android: TalkBack: swipe row by row. Double-tap 'Call back' when it is shown.
- Touch target. Web: Rows are at least 63 tall. A trailing IconButton at size 32 gets 48 through eq-touch. Android: Rows are at least 63dp. PlainIconButton is 48dp with minimumInteractiveComponentSize.
- Contrast. Web: Type text/primary 12.6:1, meta and time text/secondary 5.7:1, missed icon text/danger 6.2:1 on white. Dark on #1F1F1F: 10.9, 6.7 and 5.1:1. Android: Same tokens and ratios. The call-back icon is text/action green, 2.85:1 on white in light (brand green), lime 13.7:1 in dark.
- State. Web: Missed is said in the label, so red is not the only signal. Android: Same: the label says 'Missed Call'.
- Motion. Web: None. Android: None.

Known accessibility gaps:
- CallHistoryList in Rows.kt: itemCount defaults to -1, so unless the caller passes it TalkBack gets no call count.
- Accepted brand decision: the Compose call-back button (CallHistoryRow in Rows.kt) is text/action #00B140 on white, 2.85:1 in light mode, under 3:1 for icons.

Example: Directions
```tsx
<SectionHeader size="label" inset={22}>Call history</SectionHeader>
<CallHistoryList>
  <CallHistoryRow direction="incoming" meta="Today • 30 Sec." time="02:30 PM" />
  <CallHistoryRow direction="missed" meta="Yesterday" time="11:04 AM" />
  <CallHistoryRow direction="outgoing" meta="12 July • 2 Min." time="06:15 PM" />
</CallHistoryList>
```
```kotlin
SectionHeader(title = "Call history", size = SectionHeaderSize.Label, inset = 22.dp)
CallHistoryList {
    CallHistoryRow(CallDirection.Incoming, meta = "Today • 30 Sec.", time = "02:30 PM")
    CallHistoryRow(CallDirection.Missed, meta = "Yesterday", time = "11:04 AM")
    CallHistoryRow(CallDirection.Outgoing, meta = "12 July • 2 Min.", time = "06:15 PM")
}
```

Example: With trailing
```tsx
<CallHistoryRow direction="incoming" meta="Today • 2 Min." time="03:21 PM"
  trailing={<IconButton icon="play" label="Play recording" size={32} iconSize={20} />} />
```
```kotlin
CallHistoryList {
    // Compose: no custom trailing slot; onCallClick adds the only trailing button (call back, not play)
    CallHistoryRow(CallDirection.Incoming, meta = "Today • 2 Min.", time = "03:21 PM", onCallClick = {})
}
```

Put the query back in no-results copy and suggest what to try. Don't: Don't crop or recolour the 3D illustrations. Don't show an action when the list fills from elsewhere; if the add button is pinned below, leave it off. Anatomy: 1. Container: Centred column that fills the empty list area. (full width · padding 32 web / 24 Compose · centred) 2. Illustration: Optional 3D illustration on top. (Asset 96dp (Compose: a 96 slot) · decorative) 3. Title: Says what the feature does or what is missing. (subheading · text/primary · 16 below the art) 4. Body: Explains the empty state or suggests what to try. (captionWrap · text/secondary · max 260 web · 4 above) 5. Action: Optional filled button. (Button md 36 · 20 above web / 16 Compose) 6. IllustrationHeader: Large centred art at the top of a settings detail screen. (Asset 160dp by default · padding 8 top, 16 bottom · decorative) Accessibility: - Role. Web: The title is an h2 and the body a p. Illustrations are , so they are decorative. With announce, the container is role="status". Android: The title is heading(). EqualAssetImage has contentDescription null by default, so the art is skipped. With announce, the column is a polite liveRegion. - Name. Web: The action button is named by actionLabel. Android: The button is named by actionLabel. - Keyboard. Web: Only the action is focusable: Tab, then Enter/Space. Android: TalkBack: swipe title → body → button, double-tap to act. - Touch target. Web: The md Button is 36px tall with eq-touch, so the hit area is 48. Android: EqualButton applies minimumInteractiveComponentSize (48dp). - Contrast. Web: Title text/primary 12.6:1 and body text/secondary 5.7:1 on bg/surface (12.3 and 5.7:1 on bg/primary). The primary button is 2.85:1 in light (accepted brand decision); dark is black on lime. Android: Same tokens. - State. Web: Pass announce when it replaces a list after a search or filter; then it is read once. Otherwise it is not announced. Android: Same: announce adds a polite liveRegion. - Motion. Web: None. Android: None. Known accessibility gaps: - EmptyState with announce (Dialog.tsx): role="status" is mounted together with its text, so many screen readers skip it. Render it into a persistent live region (Announce) instead. - Accepted brand decision: primary buttons put text/on-action white on button/primary #00B140 in light mode, 2.85:1 for 14sp text (Button.css / Buttons.kt). Try a name or number.") ``` Example: Illustration header ```tsx ``` ```kotlin IllustrationHeader(asset = EqualAssets.IllustrationSilentMode) RowGroup { ToggleRow( label = "Mute Promotional Calls", description = "Equal AI Assistant can identify Promotional Calls and automatically mute them", descriptionWraps = true, checked = true, onCheckedChange = {}, ) } ```
